## Discovery 3 — Bounded minimum-norm recovery for full Gaussian source divergence

Verified: GaussianDivergenceRecovery constructs R f = sum_{n>=1} n^(-1) D P_n f for EVERY ambient Gaussian-L2 target f. Orthogonal summability and the closed divergence graph are proved from the complete actual number-sector decomposition. Thus (R f, f-P0 f) belongs to the full source divergence graph without assuming f is Malliavin differentiable.

R is a genuine bounded linear operator with ||R f||<=||f||. Its exact energy is ||R f||²=sum_{n>=1} n^(-1)||P_n f||². It is perpendicular to every divergence-free field and has minimum norm among all source divergence preimages of f-P0 f. The full source divergence range is exactly {f: inner gaussianOne f=0}.

The adjoint gives another substantive identity: if (f,g) belongs to the FULL closed derivative graph, R* g=f-P0 f. This bounded adjoint is a potential-recovery operator, not the unbounded Malliavin derivative itself. It demonstrates why naming an arbitrary bounded integration map and taking its adjoint does not automatically reconstruct the full derivative.

Mathematical significance: integration-first source recovery is available on the entire centered L2 target, with one inverse number weight. It connects the Gaussian chaos energy, Poincare estimate, closed unbounded adjunction, orthogonal kernel decomposition and minimum-norm inverse. This is classical source Hodge/pseudoinverse mathematics, newly verified through the repository's actual graph infrastructure; no novelty claim.

Limitations: this is full ambient Gaussian source divergence, not predictable Ito representation, not an intrinsic IBM observable domain, and not spatial H^-1 regularity. ## Discovery 17 — exponential probes are total in Poisson L2

For a strictly positive rate, a scalar Poisson L2 class orthogonal to exp(theta N) for every real theta is zero. Consequently the closed linear span of this actual exponential family is the entire scalar L2 space.

## Discovery 21 — full Poisson divergence recovery

For every strictly positive rate, every actual scalar Poisson L2 target f has a genuine maximal divergence preimage of f minus its mean. The recovery is a bounded linear map into the rate-weighted field L2 space, with norm at most one. The divergence range is exactly the centered subspace. Its preimage is unique among all maximal-domain fields, using the previously proved zero divergence kernel.

Construction: normalize the weighted field ladder and sum the scalar coefficient at degree n+1 divided by sqrt(n+1). The complete scalar basis proves square summability; field orthogonality proves convergence. Closedness of the actual maximal divergence graph identifies the limit. The inverse energy is the sum of squared inverse coefficients, and is bounded by the scalar target energy. The zero scalar coefficient is proved equal to the actual Poisson integral.

This extends discovery 12 from finite positive polynomial expansions to all centered L2, without differentiability assumptions on the target. Gaussian and Poisson both have bounded centered source recovery, while their kernels differ: Poisson recovery is unique; the multidirectional Gaussian recovery selects a minimum-norm solution among solenoidal alternatives. No process-level predictable Poisson representation theorem follows from this source result.

## Discovery 22 — sharp full-domain Poisson Poincare and divergence coercivity

Every genuine maximal difference graph pair (f,g) satisfies norm(f minus its mean) <= norm(g) in the rate-weighted field space. Thus the variance is at most lambda times the ordinary Poisson expectation of the squared forward difference. The normalized first Charlier mode lies in the actual difference graph and attains equality, so the constant is sharp.

Every genuine maximal divergence graph pair (u,f) also satisfies norm(u)<=norm(f). The proof uses the unique all-L2 recovery from discovery 21, with no finite-polynomial restriction on either inequality. The sharper bound norm(R f)<=norm(centered f) follows by uniqueness, and adjoint duality with this recovered field gives the Poincare estimate.

Reusable principle: bounded centered divergence recovery plus adjoint graph duality yields full-domain Poincare; injective divergence additionally yields coercivity. This connects the actual Gaussian/Poisson source program at the level of closed operators, beyond matching finite eigenvalues.

## Discovery 23 — quartic singularities persist at nonzero data

Verified general obstruction: if two source vectors have disjoint actual L4 images, the quartic normal map satisfies A(u+a v)=A(u)+a^3 A(v). For every nonzero v, the inverse violates every proposed local linear modulus at A(u), not only at the origin. All identities are equalities of actual Lp classes and genuine dual maps.

A concrete counterexample is constructed in L4 of a positive-rate Poisson law with the identity bounded source map. The indicators of count zero and count one are nonzero and disjoint. The image of the first indicator is a proved nonzero dual datum, yet every dual neighborhood contains inverse perturbations violating any linear bound. This is a nonlinear Banach normal equation on the actual Poisson probability space; the identity map here is not asserted to be the maximal Poisson divergence.

The origin homogeneity obstruction from discoveries 4 and 9 was not the only possible degeneracy. A positive nondegenerate Hessian/coercivity condition would require a separate theorem and can fail along disjoint images.

## Discovery 24 — all-degree normalized Wick metric transfer for fractional sources

For any two unit Gaussian source directions with nonnegative correlation, their degree n+1 Wick distance squared lies between (n+1)! times the source distance squared and (n+1)(n+1)! times that distance squared. This is a two-sided comparison in actual Gaussian L2, derived from mixed Wick moments and scalar power bounds on correlations in [0,1].

For the repository's actual fractional Gaussian realization, every positive-time direction has strictly positive norm and can be normalized to unit variance. Its covariance is proved nonnegative for all nonnegative times, so the comparison applies at every pair of positive times and every positive Wick degree, for every 0<H<1. No independence, invertible covariance matrix, or time generator is assumed.

This extends discovery 6 beyond second chaos and supplies a concrete Gaussian/fractional transfer of mean-square geometry. It says that normalized higher Wick degrees retain source metric roughness up to explicit constants. It does not by itself prove sample-path Holder exponents, sharp full-past prediction asymptotics, or behavior of normalization at time zero.

## Discovery 25 — representative Fubini without a uniform majorant

On finite parameter and source measures, integrable scalar L2 sections with a jointly strongly measurable scalar representative have an integrable product representative. Their scalar column integrals equal the Bochner L2 integral almost everywhere and themselves belong to actual L2. No uniform pointwise L2 majorant or independently supplied column L2 class is required.

Proof: Cauchy–Schwarz controls the integral of the absolute test pairing by norm(V) norm(v_x), making every such product pairing integrable from Bochner integrability. The constant test class gives product L1 integrability and almost-everywhere column integrability. Indicator test classes and justified scalar Fubini identify all set integrals of the Bochner class and the column integral; integrable-function uniqueness gives actual almost-everywhere equality. L2 membership then transfers from the Bochner class.

This is a reusable bridge between quotient-valued integration and actual scalar observables. It strengthens the earlier BochnerL2Fubini rule in the scalar finite-measure setting, and directly targets the remaining per-clock IBM cubic representative gap. It does not assert infinite-source-measure versions, arbitrary vector-valued representative uniqueness, joint clock L2 moments, or stochastic integration.

## Discovery 49 — weighted coercivity fails at every Poisson L4 identity-source datum

For every positive Poisson rate and every actual F in L4 of its count law, no c>0 satisfies c||w||_4 <= ||F w||_2 for all source directions w. This includes representatives with no zero coordinates.

The proof computes the weighted map on every indicator atom: output norm to the fourth power is F(n)^4 p_n^2, while input norm to the fourth power is p_n. A hypothetical lower bound forces c^4 <= p_n F(n)^4 for every n. Actual L4 integrability makes that sequence summable and hence convergent to zero, contradicting c>0. All products are actual Lp classes, and positivity of each Poisson atom is used legitimately.

Significance: discovery 47's sufficient Lipschitz condition cannot hold anywhere for the infinite-dimensional Poisson L4 identity source, even though discovery 48 realizes it on its constant source subspace. This is an applicability obstruction, not yet a proof that the inverse is singular everywhere. The latter requires a separate perturbation argument.

## Discovery 50 — the actual Poisson L4 quartic inverse is nowhere locally Lipschitz

For every positive Poisson rate, every dual datum f0, every real proposed linear constant K and every positive dual radius r, there is another actual dual datum f with ||f-f0||<r and K||f-f0|| < ||A^-1(f)-A^-1(f0)||. The inverse is the already verified complete-space quartic normal equivalence for the L4 identity source. Thus no datum admits a local linear inverse stability bound.

This proof does not infer singularity from failure of a sufficient condition. It constructs normalized atom directions of unit source norm. For every F in actual Poisson L4, x_n=F(n)||indicator_n||_4 tends to zero in absolute value, because x_n^4 is the summable actual quartic atom energy. The exact nonlinear perturbation is A(F+a w_n)-A(F)=((x_n+a)^3-x_n^3) A(w_n), with ||A(w_n)||<=1. Choosing a_n=1/(n+1) makes data changes small relative to the source increment and gives the genuine inverse counterexample at every datum.

Significance: the earlier zero and disjoint-support singularities extend to all data, including sources with strictly positive representatives. This corrects the prospective idea that avoiding zero coordinates might restore local Lipschitz stability for the infinite Poisson L4 identity source. It does not contradict the constant-subspace positive example or apply automatically to arbitrary source embeddings.

It does not assert the same behavior for arbitrary infinite-dimensional source embeddings.

For every nonnegative Poisson rate lambda and every real theta, the strictly positive density exp(theta n-lambda(exp(theta)-1)) changes the actual count law exactly into Poisson(lambda exp(theta)). ## Discovery 55 — exact Gaussian–Poisson square-root density geometry

Actual square-root densities of the Poisson exponential tilts are constructed as unit-norm vectors in the original Poisson L2. Their inner product is exp(-lambda/2 (exp(theta/2)-exp(eta/2))^2); their squared Hellinger distance is twice one minus this affinity. The parameter sqrt(lambda) exp(theta/2) is proved equal to the square root of the actual tilted rate.

Actual normalized Gaussian exponential vectors G(a)=exp(-a^2) exp(a x) in the physical standard Gaussian L2 have norm one and inner product exp(-(a-b)^2/2). Thus the Poisson tilt square-root density affinity matches these Gaussian vectors exactly at square-root rate coordinates. Every finite linear combination has the same inner product under this map. The Gaussian vectors have the classical square-root density form for unit-variance location tilts with means 2a; identification of shifted Gaussian laws is not a new formal theorem here. No equality of the Gaussian and Poisson laws is asserted.

Significance: physical Poisson rate geometry has an exact Gaussian kernel after the square-root transformation, despite different multiplication and entropy structures. This is a second precise Gaussian–Poisson bridge, involving density geometry rather than identifying arbitrary stochastic processes or source products. A full unitary extension for this particular positive-parameter family is not proved here.

## Discovery 56 — physical tilt composition and exact entropy asymmetry

Actual Poisson exponential tilts form an additive parameter action: tiltedRate(tiltedRate(lambda,theta),eta)=tiltedRate(lambda,theta+eta), with the opposite parameter returning the original rate. Their strictly positive density functions satisfy the exact multiplicative cocycle, so this is a physical change-of-measure composition principle.

The ordered reverse relative entropy is lambda(exp(theta)-theta-1), while the forward value is lambda(theta exp(theta)-exp(theta)+1). At theta=2 their difference is exactly 4 lambda, and is nonzero at every positive rate. The two measures are the original law and its actual exponential tilt; the inverse-rate theorem identifies the reversed pair legitimately.

Significance: the exact symmetric affinity geometry of discovery 55 does not determine ordered physical relative entropy. This gives a concrete limitation on density-Hilbert geometry transfer, consistent with the earlier Gaussian/Poisson multiplication and entropy obstructions. No general entropy inequality is asserted.

The actual Poisson birth/death expression Gf(n)=lambda Delta f(n)+n(f(n-1)-f(n)) is linked pointwise to minus the genuine maximal divergence/difference composition on every admitted number-domain triple. Its generator carre du champ is half the forward plus backward jump energy. A sum-of-squares decomposition proves Gamma2>=Gamma/2 for every count function; linear count functions show that 1/2 is the optimal uniform pointwise coefficient.

Separately, the actual forward source energy lambda(Delta f)^2 satisfies an exact Bochner identity: forwardBochner=forwardEnergy+lambda Gamma(Delta f), hence a coefficient-one lower bound. This forward energy differs from the generator carre du champ pointwise. For actual exponential probes their integrals agree, and both equal the genuine maximal source energy.

For every positive rate and every C>=0, an exponential probe belongs to both full source graphs, has integrable Gamma and finite entropy integrand, and violates EntSq<=C integral Gamma. The same probes violate the bound using forward energy. The diffusion exponential chain rule fails at count zero, and therefore fails almost everywhere equality under the actual positive-mass Poisson law. Positive quadratic curvature and a forward Bochner bound cannot replace the missing diffusion algebra in a Gaussian entropy argument.

## Discovery 99 — full divergence extends boundedly over completed linear Gaussian fields

Take the actual Gaussian vector L2 closure of finite rank fields a times X_b. Every field in this native completed space lies in the original full divergence domain, and its divergence is exactly 2 R adjoint applied to the field. Its scalar output lies in the genuine second number sector. No divergence operator or graph is redefined.

The exact derivative is twice the global gradient projection, canonical recovery returns that gradient component, and output energy is twice its squared norm. Thus divergence norm is at most square root of two times field norm on this completed space; its kernel is exactly the zero gradient component. Legitimate unconditional sums of such fields preserve the actual graph and the corresponding scalar sum.

Significance: the finite quadratic matrix Hodge formulas now extend to a closed space of genuine linear Gaussian fields, allowing controlled infinite second-chaos outputs. The proof uses actual finite-rank graphs and closure under the bounded 2 R adjoint map. It does not claim boundedness of full divergence on all vector L2 fields, or a separate named Hilbert-Schmidt matrix equivalence or surjectivity onto every second-chaos scalar target.

For every unit Gaussian source direction, constructed actual centered polynomial observables F=X+(X²-1)/2 and G=X-(X²-1)/2. These observables mix degrees one and two; they are not jointly Gaussian random variables. The result does not refute the pure second-chaos product conjecture or weaker source-dependent stability estimates. Pure-degree structure is a substantive hypothesis worth preserving in the next quartic source investigation.

Every terminal L2 observable generated by the future response has exactly the same conditional projection against the whole response history as against the current response coordinate. All Wick degrees have the exact projected direction and forecast energy formula, including zero rate, zero time and degenerate cases. The linear response is identified with the genuine predictable Ito integral of the causal exponential profile. Its innovation direction is orthogonal to every past direction; the actual Gaussian innovation is independent of the entire uncountable past-response process as a product-valued random variable.

A reusable theorem shows that any two observation families with the same linear source forecast give identical prediction for every single-terminal Gaussian L2 observable. This generalizes the prior sufficient-coordinate theorem and avoids imposing normalization or nondegeneracy.

## Discovery 113 — sharp distance of full Gaussian recovery from compact operators

Preserved and checked the proof already present at the start of incoming discovery: `Foundation/GaussianRecoveryCompactApproximationGap.lean`. Compression through the isometric first-chaos embedding and vacuum-field adjoint sends recovery to the identity of the infinite-dimensional coefficient space. Compression preserves compactness and cannot increase operator norm. A compact operator within distance less than one of identity would be invertible by the Neumann-series criterion, forcing compact identity and finite dimension, a contradiction.

Consequently every compact K has `1 ≤ ‖recoveryOperator - K‖`. Recovery has norm exactly one, so K=0 attains the bound. This completes the investigation proposed after discovery 112. Norm-convergent finite-degree recovery truncations remain compatible with this result because they retain infinite within-degree multiplicity.

Public results: `compression_recovery`, `compression_compact`, `compression_norm_bound`, `compact_endomorphism_distance`, `compact_approximation_gap`, `recoveryOperator_norm_one`, `optimal_compact_error`. No manuscript assumptions are involved. General finite-dimensional observed-source compactness still needs finite-rank observed chaos blocks.

### Independently disproved general Schur bound, and a useful repair

The block paper states a perturbation loss `eta_xx + 4 eta_xy²/m0 + 2 ‖b0‖² eta_yy/m0²`. With unit interior block, take H0=[[2,1],[1,1]] and H=[[2,11/10],[11/10,1]]. Both are positive definite: their Schur complements are 1 and 79/100. The claimed lower bound is 24/25, greater than 79/100. Here eta_xx=eta_yy=0 and eta_xy=1/10, satisfying the interior hypothesis. The omitted cross term is linear in eta_xy.

## Discovery 146 — every pure pseudo-moment order p>2 has an explicit negative polynomial square

`Foundation/PseudoMomentPositivity.lean` independently proves a uniform obstruction from the manuscript's stated moments, with no manuscript theorem assumed. Let E be any real linear functional on real polynomials, p>2, with E[X^n]=0 whenever p does not divide n, and let m=E[X^p] be nonzero. Lean proves the exact witness identity

`E[(X - m·X^(p-1))^2] = -2m^2 < 0`.

The diagonal terms vanish because p divides neither 2 nor 2(p-1); the cross term is the nonzero p-th moment. Both the polynomial expansion and these divisibility facts are proved. The result applies to odd and even p and either sign of the leading moment. A second theorem instantiates the leading value as p!·c·T for any c≠0 and T>0, matching the spectral-moment convention without relying on a particular sign choice. For Airy moments E[X²]=E[X⁴]=0 and E[X³]=-6T, a separate explicit calibration proves

`E[(X + 6T·X²)^2] = -72T²`.

This extends the earlier p=4 negative-fourth-moment diagnostic rather than presenting that special case as new. The generic polynomial-pairing lemmas also exhibit positive and negative square values from two null diagonal vectors with nonzero cross pairing. They prove that the diagonal null set is not additive in this situation: E[P²]=E[Q²]=0 but E[(P+Q)²]≠0. Consequently the whole set of zero-square vectors cannot serve as a linear seminorm kernel. This does not rule out taking the linear radical of a bilinear pairing or constructing an indefinite space with additional topology.

Those three properties cannot hold together for p>2 at positive time and nonzero leading coefficient. The explicit polynomial witness already belongs to the asserted polynomial class. Thus positivity on that entire class is contradicted, not merely left as an unspecified norm construction problem.

Scope is essential. The abstract and lines 383–410 explicitly acknowledge indefinite pairings and distinguish non-degeneracy from positivity. The new obstruction is compatible with signed pseudo-expectations, formal spectral moments, triangular Appell expansions, and potentially non-degenerate algebraic integrand pairings. It does not by itself refute their algebraic recurrence identities or integrand uniqueness under a separately justified pairing. A valid completion/continuity result would need a genuine positive topology and correctly stated function class, or a rigorous indefinite-space formulation; it cannot use E[F²] as a positive squared norm on all the asserted polynomials. ## Discovery 147 — construct and characterize the valid polynomial pseudo-Stein functional

`Foundation/PseudoPolynomialStein.lean` constructs an actual real linear functional `expectation p a` on all real polynomials. It is not a positive measure or a Hilbert-space expectation. Its coefficient moments are defined by the terminating recurrence

`m(0)=1`,
`m(n+1)=p·a·n.descFactorial(p-1)·m(n-(p-1))`.

The polynomial functional is the finite coefficient sum `E[g]=sum_n coeff(g,n)·m(n)`, implemented using Mathlib's actual polynomial linear sum. Lean proves the monomial evaluation rule and, for every p>0, the complete spectral moment formulas

`m(pk)=(pk)!·a^k/k!`, and `m(n)=0` when p does not divide n.

Both formulas follow from the recurrence rather than being assumed as manuscript axioms. In particular m(p)=p!·a. The full factorial formula uses descending-factorial identities and cancels only nonzero factorials.

For every real polynomial g, the actual constructed functional satisfies

`E[X·g]=p·a·E[derivative^[p-1] g]`.

This is the multiplication form of the manuscript's polynomial Stein identity, with a=c_p T; when p·a≠0 it has the displayed reciprocal form. The proof checks powers using the recurrence and extends by actual polynomial linearity and finite monomial decomposition. No positivity, conditional expectation, density claim, signed kernel integral, or infinite series limit is used. A further uniqueness theorem shows that normalization E[1]=1 and this polynomial Stein identity characterize the entire polynomial functional: any real linear functional with those properties equals the constructed one.

The construction simultaneously proves a useful contrast: for p>2 and a≠0 this very same functional is not square-positive, by the verified witness of discovery 146. Thus the algebraic Stein characterization and the absence of a positive squared norm coexist in one actual object. This preserves a valid algebraic part of the source while excluding the incompatible positive-completion interpretation; it is not a blanket rejection of pseudo-moment mathematics.

It also proves that this condition is equivalent to the existence of an actual Gaussian-coordinate integral functional equal to E_(p,a), including the degenerate coordinate h=0. ### Mathematical connection — the pure-order boundary and Marcinkiewicz's theorem

A question-led primary-source check located Eugene Lukacs, *Some extensions of a theorem of Marcinkiewicz* (1958), [Theorem B in the introduction and Theorem 1](https://msp.org/pjm/1958/8-3/pjm-v8-n3-p11-p.pdf). The paper states and reproves the obstruction to exp(P(t)) being a characteristic function when P is a polynomial of degree greater than two. The verified pure-order boundary here is an elementary moment-level special case associated with a single nonquadratic cumulant; it is not a newly discovered general probability theorem. The repository proof does not establish the full Marcinkiewicz result for mixed polynomial logarithms. Adding a positive quadratic/Gaussian term removes the zero-second-moment shortcut, so the present negative-square witness cannot simply be reused unchanged. This exposes a substantive next mathematical question: determine exact finite-degree moment-matrix positivity thresholds after adding Gaussian variance, then distinguish those finite-degree tests from global probability realizability. No external theorem is imported as a Lean axiom.

## Discovery 150 — the exact cubic-square positivity threshold and explicit boundary witnesses

`Foundation/MixedCubicThirdDegree.lean` derives the actual fifth and sixth moments from discovery 149's terminating recurrence:

`m5=10v kappa`, `m6=15v³+10kappa²`.

It proves a coefficient representation for every polynomial of degree at most three, its actual square-pairing formula, and a convenient centered basis `1, X, Y=X²-v, Z=X³-kappa-3vX`. The actual centered square pairing has Gram matrix

`[[v,kappa,0], [kappa,2v²,6v kappa], [0,6v kappa,6v³+9kappa²]]`.

The finite bilinear-form identity and the matrix determinant are verified in Lean; the determinant is

`D=12v^6-24v³ kappa²-9kappa^4`.

The complete classification, including zero and negative variance parameters, is now proved:

`(forall g with natDegree g <= 3, E[g²]>=0) iff (v>=0 and D>=0)`.

For v>0 this reduces exactly to D>=0. This is a theorem about the entire polynomial test space, not just principal minors checked in isolation. The proof uses explicit actual polynomial witnesses for necessity and a division-free completed-square identity for sufficiency. With delta=2v³-kappa² and centered coefficients c,b,a,d, Lean proves

`v delta E[q²] = v delta c² + delta(vb+kappa a)² + (delta a+6v² kappa d)² + v D d²`.

Nonnegative D at positive v implies strictly positive delta. Necessity does not assume this away: when delta=0 a separate cubic has square value `-48v^6`. When delta>0 the determinant witness has square value `delta D`. Thus no singular Schur-complement division or unproved positive-semidefinite criterion is used. Mathlib's determinant formula verifies D, while the full positivity equivalence is established directly through the actual polynomial functional.

The general determinant witness has centered coefficients `(0,6v kappa²,-6v² kappa,delta)`. At v=kappa=1 it is proved equal to the original cubic `X³-6X²+3X+5`, closing the earlier -21 benchmark as a specialization of the general criterion. The stronger cubic test therefore sharpens the verified quadratic threshold kappa²<=2v³ and explains the previous example through an actual Gram/Schur calculation.

## Discovery 151 — an actual three-atom probability law realizes the truncated mixed moments

`Foundation/MixedCubicAtomicRealization.lean` constructs the genuine positive measure

`mu=(1/3) delta_(-1)+(1/2) delta_0+(1/6) delta_2`

on the real line. Lean proves its normalization as an actual `IsProbabilityMeasure` instance, finite-atom integrability, and the integral formula

`integral f dmu = f(-1)/3+f(0)/2+f(2)/6`.

Integrability is established using the actual weighted Dirac measures and measure addition, not presumed from formal weights. The real polynomial integral map is defined as a linear functional from these actual integrals.

For every real polynomial g with degree at most four, its actual integral equals `MixedCubicMomentPositivity.expectation 1 1 g`. The proof verifies the powers and extends by the actual finite coefficient expansion; it covers the whole degree-four test space. In particular the moments through degree four are `(1,0,1,1,3)`, and every quadratic-square pairing agrees exactly with the mixed functional.

Later moments separate the two objects. Lean proves

`integral x^5 dmu=5`, while `E_mixed[X^5]=10`,
`integral x^6 dmu=11`, while `E_mixed[X^6]=25`.

For the same previously verified cubic W=X³-6X²+3X+5, the positive law has `integral W(x)^2 dmu=25`, whereas the mixed polynomial functional has `E_mixed[W²]=-21`. These comparisons are packaged together for one actual law and one actual polynomial functional. Thus passing every quadratic-square test can reflect a genuine truncated positive probability realization, while the later pseudo-moments remain incompatible with positivity. This is stronger than merely checking a finite moment matrix: the measure and its integrals have been constructed.

A further theorem independently rules out any positive measure whose entire polynomial integral functional equals this v=kappa=1 mixed functional. It uses the actual negative cubic square and positivity of integration; no probability normalization, signed kernel argument, or external Marcinkiewicz theorem is assumed for that obstruction. It does not claim that no positive law can match a finite initial segment; the constructed law proves precisely the opposite through degree four.

## Discovery 152 — a sharp attained sixth-moment boundary from actual finite spectral measures

`Foundation/FiniteMatrixSpectralMeasure.lean` supplies a reusable probability construction for any real symmetric finite matrix A and coordinate i. It places mass `(U_ij)^2` at the real eigenvalue lambda_j, using Mathlib's actual spectral theorem and orthogonal eigenvector matrix U. Lean proves that the weights are nonnegative and sum to one, constructs the positive measure as a finite indexed sum of weighted Dirac masses, proves its `IsProbabilityMeasure` instance and integrability, and establishes the actual integral formula. In particular,

`integral x^n dmu_(A,i) = (A^n)_(i,i)`.

These are identities for the constructed measure, not a formal moment sequence or a law inferred from a few variances. The construction does not require A itself to be positive semidefinite; symmetry supplies real nodes and squared eigenvector coordinates supply positive weights.

`Foundation/MixedCubicSharpSixthMoment.lean` uses that construction for the real symmetric Jacobi matrix

`J_t=[[0,1,0],[1,1,1],[0,1,t-5]]`

at its first coordinate. For every real t, its actual probability law has moments

`(m0,m1,m2,m3,m4,m5,m6)=(1,0,1,1,3,t,t²-8t+26)`.

All polynomial integrability and normalization are proved before the moment identities are used. No cubic-root formulas, guessed signs of weights, or unproved moment-realizability criterion is needed.

The matching universal bound is proved for every real linear polynomial functional E nonnegative on squares and with the prescribed first six values m0 through m5. The explicit boundary polynomial is

`Q_t=X³+(4-t)X²+(t-7)X+(t-5)`.

Lean proves `E[Q_t²]=m6-(t²-8t+26)`, hence

`m6 >= t²-8t+26=(t-4)²+10`.

The actual spectral probability law attains equality for every real t. Thus both the lower bound and its positive probabilistic attainment are established, rather than leaving a positivity criterion as an existence assumption. The abstract lower-bound theorem is stated for positive polynomial functionals; it therefore applies to probability integration when the relevant polynomial integral map is defined and linear. No stronger measure-theoretic hypothesis-elimination theorem is silently claimed.

For the extremal law, the integral of Q_t² is zero and Q_t vanishes almost surely, both proved using actual nonnegative integration and finite-atom integrability. This identifies its concentration on the boundary polynomial's real zeros. The law is a sum over three eigenvalue indices, so the construction has at most three atoms; no separate proof of distinct nodes or positive weight at each index is asserted.

Calibration: at t=5 the bound is 11, matching discovery 151's actual three-atom example. At t=10 the bound is 46, whereas the mixed pseudo-moment functional has m6=25. The former -21 cubic square is exactly the deficit in this sixth-moment requirement. The new result gives a positive extremal law matching moments through degree five after the necessary sixth-moment adjustment; it does not preserve or validate the entire mixed pseudo-moment sequence.

## Discovery 153 — singular cubic-square positivity can fail both measure and coordinate consistency

`Foundation/SingularTruncatedMomentObstruction.lean` constructs a real linear polynomial functional with the exact truncated values

`(m0,...,m6)=(1,0,2,4,12,32,89)`.

For R=X²-2X-2, its actual square pairing on the basis `(1,X,R,XR)` is proved to be

`E[(c+bX+aR+dXR)²]=c²+2b²+d²`.

Every polynomial of degree at most three is represented in this basis through its actual coefficients. Consequently every cubic square is nonnegative. Nevertheless,

`E[R²]=0`, while `E[(XR)²]=1`.

The null relation fails to propagate under coordinate multiplication even though R and XR are both inside the tested cubic space. This is a singular consistency obstruction, not an overlooked negative direction within the cubic square test.

`Foundation/TruncatedPolynomialIntegration.lean` supplies the necessary finite-domain bridge: integrable, matching power moments through degree d imply integrability and matching actual integrals for every polynomial of degree at most d. It uses finite coefficient expansion and actual Bochner integration, without assuming integrability of all higher polynomials.

Using this bridge at d=6, Lean proves that no positive measure on the real line with integrable powers through six can realize the displayed truncated moments. If such a measure existed, the zero integral of R² would force R=0 almost surely, hence XR=0 almost surely. Its square integral would then be zero, contradicting the required value one. Only the specified finite moments and their integrability enter the theorem; no full polynomial realization hypothesis is substituted for the truncated problem.

Two further independent algebraic/operator conclusions are proved. For any square-positive real polynomial functional, a null square annihilates every cross pairing, and its product by X must remain null. Thus no choice of higher polynomial values can extend the displayed truncated data to a globally square-positive polynomial functional; the obstruction does not depend on assigning zero moments above degree six in the particular constructed example. Also, no normed-space polynomial map preserving the stated square energies through degree three can have a linear coordinate operator implementing multiplication by X through degree two. The theorem imposes no boundedness assumption on that linear operator. A zero-norm vector would have to map to zero, whereas the required shifted vector has squared norm one.

This complements the genuine finite spectral realizations of discovery 152: positive finite Gram data cannot be promoted to a measure or an observable operator without checking singular null-relation consistency. It does not contradict the spectral construction, whose measure, normalization and moments were independently established.

Primary-literature connection: Curto and Fialkow, *Recursiveness, Positivity, and Truncated Moment Problems* (1991), explicitly distinguish nonsingular and singular truncated Hamburger positivity and develop recursive conditions for representing measures ([introduction, pp. 604–605](https://www.math.uh.edu/~hjm/v017n4/0603CURTO.pdf)). The present rational example, finite integration bridge, null-propagation lemma and coordinate obstruction are independently verified in Lean. No general theorem from that paper is imported as an axiom, and no claim of new world-level moment-problem theory is made. The primary-source check was restricted to the relevant statement/context, not a bulk proof ingestion.

## Discovery 156 — a quantitative higher-norm repair supplies genuine Lp convergence

`Foundation/HigherLpUniformIntegrability.lean` proves the restricted-norm estimate

`eLpNorm f p (mu.restrict s) <= eLpNorm f q mu * (mu s)^(1/p.toReal-1/q.toReal)`.

The hypotheses include p<=q and almost-everywhere strong measurability. No measurability of s or finiteness of the whole measure is needed for this comparison. In particular, the L4-to-L3 exponent is exactly 1/12.

For any indexed family with a finite common higher-norm bound C, a strictly positive reciprocal-exponent gap makes the right side tend uniformly to zero with the measure of s. This proves Mathlib's `UnifIntegrable` predicate directly. On a finite measure space it also proves `UniformIntegrable`, including the separate uniform global Lp bound. The finiteness of C is explicit; an infinite bound does not discharge the hypothesis.

## Discovery 157 — all Gaussian exponential and volatility power moments do not give a positive exponential volatility-square moment

`Foundation/GaussianDoubleExponential.lean` uses the actual standard Gaussian measure `GaussianCore.gamma` (Lean name `GaussianCore.γ`). For a>0 and c>0, Lean proves that

`x -> exp(c*exp(a*x))`

is not integrable under that measure. This is a statement about actual Bochner integrability, not merely a formal divergent moment series.

The proof is elementary and quantitative. For x>=6/(c*a^3), the third Taylor term gives `x^2 <= c*exp(a*x)`. Multiplying the candidate integrand by the actual Gaussian density leaves a value at least `(sqrt(2*pi))^(-1)` throughout this half-line. Hypothetical Gaussian integrability transfers to Lebesgue integrability against the density using the already verified `GaussianCore.integrable_density_mul`. In contrast, for a>0 and c>0, `exp(c*(exp(a*x))^2)` is not integrable. ## Discovery 181 — an integrated budget repairs the before-terminal exit implication

New verified module: `Foundation/CorridorIntegratedExit.lean`, imported by the root library. This supplies a useful conditional repair to the finite-time exit inference examined in `ResearchSources/Incoming/corridor_analysis.tex`:229–233.

For a continuous concentration curve rho on [s,t], actual right derivatives q on (s,t), an integrable loss bound g on [s,t], and q<=-g, Lean proves

`rho(t) <= rho(s)-integral_s^t g`.

The proof uses the pinned one-sided derivative comparison theorem with all continuity, derivative and integrability hypotheses explicit. It does not require integrability of the actual derivative q. The one-sided formulation can admit corners when the required right derivative and inequality are independently established; it does not assume that an arbitrary finite maximum has a full derivative.

If the accumulated loss exceeds rho(s)-a at some t<T, the module proves rho(t)<a and provides an exit time in [s,T). A non-strict budget inequality gives only rho(t)<=a. Conversely, if rho(t)>=a, every certified lower loss bound of this type must have accumulated at most rho(s)-a by t.

The strict distinction is independently checked with the linear path r(x)=a+1-x on [0,1]. Its derivative is -1, its unit loss integral equals its initial margin one, and its final value is exactly a. It never falls strictly below a in that interval. Thus equality of the budget and margin does not by itself give strict exit from the source's concentrated case, which includes rho=a.

The module then computes actual budgets for the coupled scalar profile of discovery 180. Define the polynomial loss extension

`quotedLoss_epsilon(x)=(1/4)*(1-rho_epsilon(x))=epsilon/8+epsilon*x/16`.

For every x<1, this equals the actual quoted source expression lambda(x)^2*(1-rho_epsilon(x)). The source expression is independently proved interval-integrable on every [0,t] with 0<=t<=1. Equality of interval integrals uses congruence on the open interval and the null-singleton property of Lebesgue measure. It therefore does not assume that the singular energy/frequency has a physical value at t=1 or rely on a nonintegrable default integral.

The exact identities are

`integral_0^t sourceLoss = epsilon*t/8+epsilon*t^2/32`,

`integral_0^t actualLoss = epsilon*t/4`, with `actualLoss=-rho_epsilon'`,

`rho_epsilon(0)-rho_epsilon(t)=integral_0^t actualLoss`.

The initial margin over threshold 1-epsilon is epsilon/2. At the terminal time the guaranteed-loss integral is 5*epsilon/32 and the actual concentration loss is epsilon/4. For epsilon>0, Lean checks

`0 < 5*epsilon/32 < epsilon/4 < epsilon/2`.

Every prefix guaranteed-loss integral for 0<=t<=1 and every prefix actual-loss integral remains below the initial margin. The small guaranteed budget alone would not prove absence of exit for an arbitrary trajectory, since actual decay could be faster; here the exact actual-loss identity and the separately verified no-exit theorem provide that conclusion for the model. The repaired criterion and the scalar diagnostic are therefore consistent, with the missing before-terminal loss budget quantitatively identified.

## Discovery 182 — positive spectral moments identify the missing kinetic constraint

New verified module: `Foundation/SpectralEnergyInterpolation.lean`, imported by the root library. This connects the positive-moment branch of the verified library with the critical-energy bookkeeping used in the incoming Navier–Stokes manuscripts.

For a finite index set, nonnegative frequencies w_i and real amplitudes a_i, define actual positive spectral moments

`M_n=sum_i w_i^n*a_i^2`, with `K=M_0`, `E=M_1`, `Q=M_2`, `D=M_3`.

Lean proves all required nonnegativity and two actual finite Cauchy–Schwarz estimates, E^2<=K*Q and Q^2<=E*D. The second follows by multiplying the amplitudes by sqrt(w), with the square-root identities checked on the nonnegative frequency support. Combining them, treating E=0 separately before cancellation, gives

`E^3 <= K^2*D`.

Constant-frequency data attain equality. No signed pseudo-moment functional or unproved positivity assumption is used.

For any nonnegative K,D and E>0 satisfying that interpolation inequality, an independently checked scalar argument yields

`E <= K*sqrt(D/E)`.

Thus, with lambda=sqrt(D/E), simultaneous caps K<=B and lambda<=L give E<=B*L. The result identifies a condition the scalar profile of discovery 180 lacks. If that profile's E,D satisfy interpolation with any nonnegative kinetic quantity K, its actual lambda=1/2 forces K>=2*E. The genuine finite-time energy limit then makes a fixed cap on K impossible. Lean proves this exclusion both for arbitrary scalar K satisfying interpolation and for any proposed finite positive spectral representation with bounded zeroth moment.

This does not exclude the profile merely by spectral positivity. The module constructs an explicit 32-sector weighted spectral realization preserving the source energy accounting: for the positive sector energies E_j from discovery 180, take w_j=1/2 and a_j=sqrt(2*E_j). It proves each critical contribution w_j*a_j^2=E_j and the general moment identity

`M_n = 2*(1/2)^n*E`.

Consequently K=2E, M_1=E and M_3=D exactly. The scalar model saturates interpolation at this necessarily growing kinetic moment. Its previous 32-sector concentration accounting is preserved; what fails is a uniform kinetic cap. These are positive finite weighted spectra, not a construction of spatial Fourier vector fields or a Navier–Stokes solution. A continuum Fourier/Sobolev identification and an actual kinetic-energy inequality remain separate formal obligations.

The module also independently checks derivative-weight bookkeeping. Multiplying amplitudes by sqrt(w) raises the moment index by one, while multiplying by w raises it by two. In particular,

`M_1(w*a)=M_3(a)`.

This is the finite weighted norm identity relevant to testing against a full |grad|u rather than u. A conditional lemma proves that a supplied product bound with factors sqrt(E), sqrt(D) and sqrt(M_1(w*a)) becomes C*sqrt(E)*D. The lemma performs the norm substitution; it does not prove the manuscript's trilinear estimate, cone hypothesis or a continuum operator bridge.

`I(A,B)<=C*J(A,B) iff B<=C^2*A`.

## Discovery 184 — proper spectral integrals satisfy interpolation on arbitrary measure spaces

New verified module: `Foundation/SpectralMomentIntegrals.lean`, imported by the root library. This extends the finite spectral argument to actual integrals and L2 equivalence classes, rather than assuming a continuum interpretation of finite sums.

Let mu be any measure, w and a real almost-everywhere strongly measurable functions, and w>=0 almost everywhere. Assume only the endpoint integrability conditions

`integrable(a^2)` and `integrable(w^3*a^2)`.

No finite-measure or sigma-finite-measure hypothesis is imposed. The real moments are M_n=integral w^n*a^2. The module independently proves integrability of every moment integrand for n<=3. Its pointwise bound is w^n<=1+w^3 on the nonnegative frequency support, so the proper integrable dominator is a^2+w^3*a^2. It does not use an integrable constant on an infinite measure space or silently assign default values to divergent middle moments.

The endpoint and middle integrability conditions produce genuine L2 elements represented by a, w*a, sqrt(w)*a, and w*sqrt(w)*a. Frequencies need not be bounded. These are justified weighted multiplier domains, not an assumption that products of arbitrary L2 functions stay in L2.

where K=M_0, E=M_1, Q=M_2 and D=M_3 are all proper finite integral values. A separate scalar lemma combines these inequalities, handling E=0 before cancellation, to prove

The coupled scalar blow-up profile from discovery 180 therefore cannot have any such measure-space spectral representation with uniformly bounded zeroth moment, provided its first and third moments are identified with that profile and the explicit measurability/integrability hypotheses hold. This generalizes the finite exclusion without asserting an actual Navier–Stokes kinetic-energy inequality or a Fourier/Sobolev identification.

The derivative-weight identity is also checked at the integral level:

The module separately proves integrability of the weighted test integrand w*(w*a)^2 from the assumed third-moment integrability. Thus the norm-shift interpretation uses proper integrals. It is not merely an equality between two possible default Bochner values.

The source explicitly assumes closability of the gradient on the smooth compactly supported core. Its proof separates the zero coefficient from the positive coefficient, converts the energy-Cauchy condition to derivative Cauchy convergence in complete L2, and applies the gradient hypothesis. ### 410 — an actual smooth compactly supported jet

`Foundation/SmoothAtomicJet.lean` constructs a real smooth bump equal to1 near0 and the function f(x)=x*bump(x). ### 411 — regular atomic probability: derivative descent and form closability fail

`Foundation/AtomicGradientObstruction.lean` uses the actual Dirac law mu=delta_0, with native probability and regularity instances. Every real function belongs to every Lp(mu) class. Two actual L2 classes agree exactly when their representatives have the same value at0.

Consequently the smooth witness410 has L2(mu) class0 but derivative value1 at the atom. A native theorem rules out even an arbitrary nonlinear map on L2(mu) classes agreeing with the ordinary derivative-class assignment on all smooth compactly supported functions. The issue is already well-definedness on the quotient, before closure of an operator graph.

The actual integral energy is E_kappa(f)=kappa*integral((f')^2,mu)=kappa*(f'(0))^2. For the constant sequence f_n=f, the input L2 classes converge to0 and all pairwise difference energies are0, while E_kappa(f_n)=kappa. Native sequential form-closability therefore fails for every nonzero coefficient, in particular every positive coefficient relevant to the seed. The zero-coefficient form is natively closable.

This proves that finite regular/Radon mass, bounded-class membership and a smooth compact core do not by themselves supply the gradient or form-closability hypothesis. The atomic law is not asserted to be an LJR diagonal law, and this example is not a counterexample to the source's explicitly conditional lemma. ### 412 — native weighted form theorem and actual operator bridge

`Foundation/WeightedFormClosability.lean` defines a core-to-input map I and a derivative map D between real modules/normed spaces, with energy kappa*norm(Dv)^2. Sequential closability means that I(v_n) tending to0 and D(v_n) tending to y force y=0.

For positive kappa, the two-index energy-Cauchy condition is equivalent to the derivative sequence being Cauchy. With a complete derivative target, sequential closability implies form closability; conversely positive-coefficient form closability implies sequential closability. The zero-coefficient form is always closable.

`Foundation/ProjectedFormClosability.lean` starts with a real module core V, an input map I into a normed space X, and a derivative map D into a complete normed space Y. It assumes core maps P_i and continuous ambient input maps Q_i satisfying:

## Discoveries 423–425 — what is missing for a genuine sticky stochastic flow

User-directed investigation: can the verified operator and semigroup machinery be instantiated for an actual sticky stochastic flow? Current answer: not yet. The repository has verified abstract factor/closability results and concrete Gaussian/Brownian constructions, but no verified sticky transition family or stochastic flow of kernels. This is a missing construction and identification problem, not a mathematical nonexistence result.

### Existing foundations checked in the current pinned tree

The search covered the repository and pinned Mathlib probability/analysis sources for sticky flows, local time/Tanaka theory, martingale problems, Dirichlet-form generation and Feller semigroups. No reusable implementation of the sticky-specific objects or the general form-to-Feller-to-random-flow reconstruction was found. This records the audited local tree, not a claim about every external Lean project.

It would be incorrect to list Brownian paths themselves as entirely missing. `Foundation/IBMConstructedSources.lean` already constructs measurable continuous Brownian paths and proves `clock_isBrownian` without assuming path continuity. `Foundation/GaussianTimeProcess.lean` supplies the actual Gaussian finite-dimensional laws and independent increments. Mathlib supplies probability kernels, composition, disintegration, Ionescu–Tulcea, stopping/martingale infrastructure and Brownian predicates. The abstract Hilbert adjoint, orthogonal projection, Gaussian closed derivatives, weighted form criterion412, localization criterion418, and symmetric bounded-defect results420–421 are also available. Their existence does not identify any of those Gaussian operators with a sticky generator.

### 423 — a verified obstruction to the proposed terminal-law identification

`Foundation/StickyTerminalLawObstruction.lean` identifies the actual one-particle terminal law as Gaussian(0,T) using the existing constructed process. Its cosine integral is exp(-T/2). For the actual differential expression Lf=(1/2)f'', native differentiation gives Lcos=-(1/2)cos and L1=0. Consequently

integral((Lcos)*1,Gaussian(0,T))=-(1/2)*exp(-T/2),
integral(cos*(L1),Gaussian(0,T))=0.

These pairings differ for every finite T, including every positive time. The tests are bounded and smooth. Thus the Brownian half-Laplacian with these actions cannot be treated as symmetric under the finite-time observation law merely because it is symmetric under its Lebesgue reference measure. This independently resolves the concrete diagnostic left at422.

The selected manuscript's setup at1059–1085 uses the observation law mu_x, while its convention417–493 imports generator symmetry for m_theta,n; its P1 additionally asks for a Dirichlet form generated by that generator under mu_x. The new theorem exposes an obstruction to that literal generator/reference-law identification already at one particle. It does not show that the Gaussian derivative energy is unclosable, does not refute the abstract symmetric-factor lemma, and does not rule out a different associated weighted generator or a correctly chosen stationary/reference measure.

### 424 — deterministic local-time clock infrastructure constructed in Lean

`Foundation/StickyTimeChangeClock.lean` takes a nonnegative parameter kappa and a continuous nondecreasing function L:[0,infinity)->[0,infinity) with L(0)=0. It constructs A(t)=t+kappa*L(t) as an actual order isomorphism, not a postulated inverse. Strict monotonicity follows from the t term; surjectivity follows by the intermediate value theorem and A(t)>=t.

The actual inverse tau satisfies A(tau(t))=t, tau(A(t))=t, tau(t)<=t, continuity, monotonicity, and

tau(t)-tau(s)<=t-s for s<=t.

This is ready to accept a proved local-time path. It does not assert that an arbitrary L is local time, that the random inverse is jointly measurable or a stopping-time family, or that B(tau(t)) is Markov or sticky. Local-time occupation identities, normalization constants, strong Markov/time-change results and the resulting speed measure still need construction. In particular kappa has not been silently identified with a published stickiness parameter under an unverified local-time convention.

### 425 — consistent higher-collision data constructed in Lean

`Foundation/StickyCollisionRates.lean` uses a finite characteristic measure nu on [0,1], represented as the interval subtype. With zero-based indices it constructs

r(k,l)=integral(q^k*(1-q)^l,nu), corresponding to positive counts(k+1,l+1).

Native results prove boundedness and integrability of every weight, nonnegativity of every rate, the consistency identity r(k,l)=r(k+1,l)+r(k,l+1), and r(0,0)=nu([0,1]). Two explicit Dirac characteristic measures, at0 and at1/2, have the same pair rate r(0,0)=1 but different triple-splitting rates r(1,0)=0 and1/2. Thus a general higher-particle hierarchy is not specified by its pair stickiness alone. A chosen special one-parameter family may of course impose additional structure.

This proves the rate algebra only. It does not supply the drift/zero-count extension of the full generator parameters, a martingale problem solution, a Feller semigroup, or an existence theorem for either corresponding stochastic flow.

### Missing foundations and a construction sequence

Distinguish observation laws from reversible reference laws. Prove the intended consistency statements with the correct normalization. | Native obstruction423; existing singular-measure diagnostics397–399. |
| Sticky diffusion or collision form | Construct local time and occupation/Tanaka identities plus the stochastic inverse-clock theorem; alternatively construct the correct closed Markovian form with collision traces and boundary conditions. | Continuous Brownian paths already exist; deterministic clock424. The ordinary derivative with an atomic energy is not an acceptable shortcut, by411–417. |

Neither scalar pair data nor a two-point construction settles this. |
| Analytic semigroup identification | Prove that the actual generator/form yields symmetric strongly continuous L2 contractions for the chosen symmetric model; establish the bounded-defect characterization of its closed form and Feller versions. | Actual abstract operators and identities420–421; the general reconstruction theorem was not found in the pinned tree. |

A genuine flow alone would not automatically verify every proposed noise-space identity. |

These stages are mathematically constructible in principle, but they are substantial theorem developments. Recording assumptions in a structure, checking a finite Markov approximation, or adjoining an axiom asserting a sticky flow would not discharge them.

For the existing symmetric operator branch, a compact-circle form construction is the most directly aligned candidate: use finite compatible reference probabilities and prove the collision-form domains before invoking factor geometry. This is a research choice, not a proved shorter formalization. A local-time construction first gives a more focused one-particle milestone, but even a genuine one-dimensional sticky diffusion does not supply the required compatible random kernel flow. In the line setting, also test whether any proposed coordinate-pushforward reference consistency is compatible with infinite Lebesgue fibers; probability-style marginal identities must not be imported without proof.

### Primary literature checked, with external results kept separate from Lean verification

[Le Jan–Raimond, Sticky flows on the circle](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211387), especially Proposition1.3/Theorem1.4 and Section3, constructs a compatible Dirichlet-form hierarchy and obtains a kernel flow through a Feller-family reconstruction theorem. This motivates the compact symmetric route; those existence/reconstruction results are not formalized by the present files.

[Howitt–Warren, Consistent families of Brownian motions and stochastic flows of kernels](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611292), equations1.1–1.5, Proposition2.1, Theorem2.1 and Section8, supplies a distinct martingale-problem route. Its positive-count characteristic-measure rates motivate425. Its collision-sensitive process existence, uniqueness and flow reconstruction are external mathematical results, not Lean axioms or verified conclusions here. The paper also makes explicit why higher-collision behavior needs more data than a pair parameter.

The newly verified pieces make the next milestones concrete: local-time/occupation infrastructure and a genuine sticky diffusion, or closed compatible collision forms for a specified symmetric circle model. Keep testing the measure and domain identifications before attempting to attach the existing operator interfaces. All manuscript files remain read-only; no Millennium or NS/YM equivalence claim follows.

## Discoveries 426–427 — reference marginal obstruction and an actual finite measured factor

The425 user-directed sticky-flow investigation left reference-measure consistency as a concrete prerequisite. At the completed proof break, selectively checked `ResearchSources/Incoming/StickyFlowNoiseLift.tex`451–473: its convention asserts coordinate-deletion pushforward consistency of sigma-finite Radon references and identifies the one-particle reference as Lebesgue. Checked `ResearchSources/Incoming/StickyFlowGammaSeed.tex`318–341, where the advertised two-particle operator/form lives on L2(R2,dxdy). No new complete manuscript proof was ingested.

Source hashes remain `A4D9D6288F44A0831E7EABC05458E0F19364D1CF308B2E0305A81D8E14DC2F04` for the noise lift and `EFFD41A21A3D72E678EAC0A7081EC037B6935FCC4CAD0C8849C98CB320A44DDC` for the seed. The question is whether the advertised real-line references can satisfy the stated marginal identity, not whether genuine sticky flows exist.

### 426 — positive product-Lebesgue mass has an infinite coordinate marginal

`Foundation/InfiniteReferenceMarginal.lean` computes the actual first-coordinate pushforward of two-dimensional product Lebesgue measure. Its mass on the compact interval[0,1] is infinity, since the discarded fiber has infinite Lebesgue mass. The same is true for every nonzero nonnegative scalar multiple of that product measure.

The native domination theorem proves the stronger statement: if an arbitrary nonnegative measure rho on R2 dominates c*dxdy for any c!=0, then its first-coordinate marginal gives infinite mass to[0,1]. Therefore that marginal is not one-dimensional Lebesgue and is not locally finite. Adding any nonnegative diagonal or other measure to the positive product component cannot repair this failure.

Thus the literal combination of the advertised one- and two-particle Lebesgue references with the stated coordinate-pushforward identity is inconsistent. If a different two-point reference is intended, its actual definition and compatibility must replace that identification. This remains a conditional obstruction for references containing a globally positive product-Lebesgue component; it does not rule out every sigma-finite reference hierarchy, coordinate compatibility of Markov transition kernels, alternative disintegrations, or the genuine LJR construction. In particular, consistency of transition laws is not the same assertion as consistency of infinite reference-measure pushforwards.

### 427 — a diagonal reference probability with exact marginals

`Foundation/DiagonalReferenceProbability.lean` constructs, for any probability measure mu and any p in[0,1], the actual measure

rho_p=(1-p)*(mu product mu)+p*diagonal_pushforward(mu).

Native theorems prove that rho_p is a probability measure, both coordinate marginals equal mu, and swapping coordinates preserves rho_p. If mu is a real probability measure with null singletons, the diagonal has mass exactly p. The actual standard Gaussian law is instantiated using its proved absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue, so the Gaussian example is not left behind an unverified atomlessness assumption.

The construction is generic in the underlying measurable space, so it can accept a separately verified compact-space probability reference. The concrete Gaussian specialization is a measured example, not a stationary sticky Brownian law or a substitute for the intended circle dynamics. The coefficient restriction p<=1 is explicit for probability and marginal consistency; diagonal-mass computations remain ordinary measure statements even outside that restriction.

### An actual input for the Hilbert factor machinery

The coordinate projections are natively measure-preserving for rho_p and mu. Using Mathlib's actual measure-preserving Lp composition,427 constructs a linear isometry J:L2(mu)->L2(rho_p). Its representative is f(x) on the first coordinate, with the equality proved almost everywhere under the actual joint measure.

The existing `HilbertRepresentation` machinery now gives a concrete bounded adjoint J* on those actual L2 spaces. A native agreement theorem proves J*Jf=f for every actual L2 input. Consequently this checkpoint instantiates the measured-isometry and bounded-adjoint part of the earlier factor interfaces without postulating marginal compatibility or an abstract unidentified law.

No generator A/B, semigroup intertwining, energy contraction, collision-form closability or core preservation is supplied by this measured construction. The adjoint is not asserted to satisfy the manuscript's derivative-energy contraction merely because it is the adjoint of an isometry. Its explicit conditional-kernel formula is also not newly proved here. The next useful analytic question is to construct that kernel or identify a closed tangential collision energy, then test compatibility with a specified generator.

### What this changes in the sticky-flow foundation plan

The reference-measure bridge has both a verified negative test and a positive finite prototype. Infinite product fibers must be handled before importing probability-style projection identities. Finite probability references with actual diagonal mass do support the desired isometric coordinate pullbacks and adjoints. This addresses one interface in425's roadmap but does not discharge the all-particle hierarchy, collision dynamics, Feller reconstruction or random kernel flow construction.

For a particular sticky model the reference weights, higher-particle partition laws and form domains still need their own constructions. The existing atomic nonclosability examples warn against assigning ordinary derivative energy to singular mass without the appropriate tangential/trace geometry. No stochastic-flow existence, full noise-space operator, continuum gap, NS/YM equivalence or Millennium conclusion is established. Continue the indefinite exploration from these concrete measure and operator facts.

### 428 — reusable continuous random-time composition

`Foundation/ContinuousRandomTimeComposition.lean` constructs the actual path X(omega,Y(xi,t)) for measurable random continuous outer and inner paths on arbitrary measurable sample spaces. Native results prove coordinate measurability, measurability into continuous-path space, continuity of every constructed path, and joint time/sample measurability. No probability, independence, Gaussianity, positivity or Hilbert-space hypothesis is required for this construction.

This is a genuinely reusable realization tool for random time changes. Independence, adaptation, stopping-time properties, stochastic integrability and model laws remain separate properties; composition alone does not supply them. It may be reused for another branch once that branch has actual measurable continuous paths.

### 429 — the actual signed-clock IBM and its conditional Gaussian law

`Foundation/SignedIBMRealization.lean` instantiates428 with the previously constructed two-sided Brownian scenery and independent Brownian clock. Its actual value is

Z_t(omega,xi)=sceneryPath(omega,clockPath(xi,t)).

No absolute value is inserted. Existing source theorems already prove Brownian behavior on both sides of the outer time axis, independence of the outer branches and independence of the entire scenery/clock paths. The new construction proves path measurability, joint measurability, continuous paths and the exact composition identity.

For every fixed clock sample,429 proves the scenery-section process is Gaussian and every finite observation vector has a Gaussian law. Its native conditional-section covariance is

(abs(C_s)+abs(C_t)-abs(C_t-C_s))/2.

The phrase conditional here denotes the proved laws on the independent scenery factor with the clock fixed; no additional identification with a regular-conditional-kernel version is claimed. Native checks give outer covariance0 at times1,-1, versus1 at their reflected times1,1. This demonstrates a concrete difference in the covariance kernels used by signed and absolute clock composition. It is not asserted to be a new proof of inequality of their unconditional path laws.

The preexisting absolute-clock construction was not incorrect: it is a different explicitly defined process. Its fixed-mollifier operator formulas must not silently be transferred to signed-clock IBM. The new signed process has not yet been connected to a singular-mollifier Ito correction, local-time formula, or the entire existing IBM derivative graph.

### Appropriate next foundations, without manufacturing completion tasks

For pseudoprocesses, a useful future project would first specify an actual signed kernel/distributional evolution and a test-function topology. A polynomial linear functional with negative square values cannot be supplied to the positive Hilbert machinery as a norm. Signed integration would require controlled total variation or a specified dual/distribution pairing; no signed path extension is claimed here, and the absence of a positive model is not a proof that every alternative fails.

For black noise, the missing object is a continuous product F_(s,t) with independent adjacent factors and the appropriate concatenation/stationarity properties. A precise first-chaos target is the centered additive L2 sector: on each interval, variables X satisfying X=E[X|F_(s,u)]+E[X|F_(u,t)] for every intermediate u. Blackness would require this sector to be trivial in the constructed continuous product. This is a formulation to formalize, not a newly verified definition/blackness theorem. In particular the manuscript's broader claims about unavailable martingale or driving-noise formulas are not adopted merely from its abstract.

For fBM, the most concrete missing realization step is a continuous modification of the already constructed process, followed by transfer of observation sigma-fields and its existing calculus. For SPDEs, an explicit linear spatial generator and mild equation is the next identification step; a nonlinear or singular equation is a further problem. Sticky construction priorities are detailed in425–427 and remain finite research opportunities, not conditions that must all be completed before other Stardust work resumes.

### Connection to Paper1 and exit from the temporary audit

The integration-first framework is already substantive for actual Gaussian and one-site Poisson L2 spaces. Closed graph/adjoint results, actual isometric pullbacks, source projections, recovery identities and localization criteria are reusable with their displayed hypotheses. The projected closability theorem418 needs input continuity, energy contraction, core compatibility and local closability; it does not become a universal realization theorem. The symmetric-factor energy theorem420 needs the actual symmetric nonnegative operators and isometric intertwining. Neither can be instantiated for an unidentified signed or black-noise object by analogy.

For example, `operatorClosure_le_closed`, `formalAdjoint_closure_left` and `operatorClosure_adjoint_eq` in `Foundation/AdjointClosure.lean` are genuine generic Paper1 tools: they work for the stated real inner-product spaces and actual closable/dense domains, with completeness where used. They do not assume Gaussianity, but they do assume the displayed positive inner-product geometry. The signed/distributional branch would need its own well-posed pairing/domain setup before importing an analogue.

New428 extends the realization toolkit without positivity or Hilbert assumptions, while429 closes a concrete process-construction gap. The audit has not declared any stochastic branch publication-complete or any manuscript headline correct. Formal verification, novelty and independent assessment remain distinct.

This completes a meaningful temporary pass over all named branches and the additional Poisson/stable gap. `Foundation/PeriodicFineSparseGram.lean` proves that the actual integer full curl Gram equals a sum over the six ordered direction pairs i<j. ### 433 — a necessary and sufficient equality criterion

`Foundation/PeriodicLiftEqualityCriterion.lean` works with the actual fine physical lattice space, A=R, B=P R^T, fine physical Gram G, Q=A B and S=A G^(-1) B. For every physical f with A f=c, it proves

f=M c if and only if G f belongs to range(B),

where M is the existing energy-minimizing lift. The reverse implication constructs the multiplier through the already proved invertibility of S; membership is not assumed from an analogy. Writing J for the norm-minimizing lift, the native consequences are

J c=M c if and only if G J c belongs to range(B),

and strict energy improvement occurs if and only if this range membership fails. Every fine-Gram eigenvector J c therefore gives equality. Global equality for every coarse physical source is equivalent to G preserving range(B). The old strict witness explicitly disproves that invariance on this actual lattice. The checkerboard equality and the strict witness thus fit one criterion.

### 434 — a feasible residual and a noncommuting projection

`Foundation/PeriodicConstrainedEnergyDescent.lean` constructs the actual linear reconstruction projection N=J A=B Q^(-1) A on fine physical fields. It fixes range(B), is idempotent, and preserves A. Native adjunction proves that every v in ker(A) is orthogonal to every N f.

Define v(f)=G f-N G f. Then A v=0, the pairing <v,G f> equals the squared fine norm of v, and v=0 if and only if f=M(A f). Thus v is the projected gradient of one half of the fine curl energy; the gradient of the full energy has the extra factor2. For every real t the actual feasible field f-t v has the same coarse average and satisfies

E(f-t v)=E(f)+t^2 E(v)-2t ||v||^2.

For nonzero v, physical positivity gives E(v)>0. The native choice t=||v||^2/E(v) yields the exact strict decrease

E(f-t v)=E(f)-||v||^4/E(v)<E(f).

This is an actual finite-dimensional constrained correction, with no assumed spectrum or external numerical solver. It is exact line minimization in this direction, not a general one-step solution. The strict witness also proves G N is not equal to N G. This is a fine-space commutator. It does not contradict the unverified prototype evidence that the two different coarse operators Q and S might commute.

### 435 — the strict witness is solved in one step

`Foundation/PeriodicExactDescentWitness.lean` specializes to the existing badSource. With j=J c=12p and the earlier verified fine fields p,a, native formulas give

G j=72p-48a, N G j=36p, v(j)=36p-48a.

j-(1/5)v(j)=M c.

It is not a convergence theorem for iterations from arbitrary fine fields, and the factor1/5 is neither a global gap nor the local conditional block Hessian spectrum.

`Foundation/SU2StaplePolar.lean` upgrades the existing explicit quaternion representation to a real linear map. S=||q|| V, S^* S=||q||^2 I, ||q||<=number of staples.

These identities use the actual complex2-by2 matrices and unit-quaternion/SU(2) equivalence, not a toy matrix model. The zero-sum case is included and never divided by its norm. `Foundation/SU2StapleTiltLaw.lean` defines X_V(A)=halfTrace(V A). ### 442 — normalized joint density, boundary marginal and native conditional-kernel certificate

`Foundation/ExponentialJointDisintegration.lean` starts with actual probability references rho and mu and a jointly measurable exponent X(p,x), integrable exponential sections, and an integrable exponential on the product reference. It defines the joint measure directly by the global density

dJ(p,x)=exp(X(p,x))/C * d(rho prod mu),

Native theorems prove pi is a probability, J=pi compProd K for the already constructed normalized exponential kernel K, J is a probability and J.fst=pi. `Foundation/BrownianZeroOccupation.lean` uses the already constructed continuous Brownian clock and the actual finite-horizon nonvanishing result448. ### 455 — a density supported on those zeros cannot create a forward clock

`Foundation/BrownianZeroClockObstruction.lean` defines a real rate q supported at the original Brownian zeros: q(t)=0 whenever t>0 and B_t!=0. On the same probability-one path event, every such q is Lebesgue-almost everywhere zero on every finite horizon, and therefore

integral_0^T q(t) dt=0.

### 458 — explicit smooth convex absolute-value approximations

`Foundation/SmoothAbsoluteApproximation.lean` constructs, for an actual positive real parameter e,

f_e(x)=sqrt(x^2+e^2),

f'_e(x)=x/sqrt(x^2+e^2),

The first and second formulas are proved to equal the actual Mathlib derivatives by ordinary differentiation. Native results establish smoothness at every order, |x|<=f_e(x)<=|x|+e, uniform error at most e, |f'_e|<=1, nonnegative curvature and |f''_e|<=1/e. Thus f_e is 1-Lipschitz and its actual derivative is 1/e-Lipschitz. No arbitrary derivative candidate is supplied to Ito.

`Foundation/BrownianTanakaApproximation.lean` uses the explicit positive sequence e_n=1/(n+1). It proves pointwise convergence of the smooth slopes to the measurable sign function, including x=0. The slope fields are dominated in absolute value by the already constructed sign field. Native L2 dominated convergence therefore gives convergence in the actual time/probability L2 space, and hence in the raw predictable domain, to sign(B_t) on (0,T]. Continuity of the verified stochastic integral gives

integral_0^T f'_(e_n)(B_t) dB_t -> N_T in L2.

The terminal uniform-error bound independently gives f_(e_n)(B_T) -> |B_T| in Gaussian L2. The limiting absolute-value class is identified almost everywhere with |clockPath(T)|. The global Lipschitz function itself is not assumed bounded; the argument uses its actual uniform approximation error on the probability space.

### 460 — a positive, monotone, L2-continuous residual

`Foundation/BrownianTanakaResidual.lean` independently defines the actual smooth curvature drifts as Gaussian-L2 Bochner integrals

A_n(T)=(1/2) integral_0^T f''_(e_n)(B_t) dt.

The existing C2 Ito theorem, instantiated with the proved actual derivatives and bounds, proves

A_n(T)=f_(e_n)(B_T)-e_n-integral_0^T f'_(e_n)(B_t) dB_t.

The deterministic initial value is e_n, so no initial-value term is silently discarded. The drift curves are genuinely integrable; their continuity is inherited from the existing bounded-curvature construction. The usual order on L2 is identified with almost-everywhere scalar order, and positive scalar multiplication is proved to preserve it locally. Bochner integration of the nonnegative curvature gives A_n(T)>=0. Positivity of the intervening interval integral also gives A_n(S)<=A_n(T) for S<=T.

Define L_T=|B_T|-N_T as an actual Gaussian L2 class. The preceding terminal and stochastic limits prove A_n(T)->L_T in L2. Closedness of the positive cone then proves L_T>=0, and closedness of the order relation proves L_S<=L_T for S<=T. Native theorems additionally prove L_0=0 and continuity of T->L_T in L2. The sign-integral L2 continuity is derived from its exact verified covariance, rather than postulated.

The displayed fixed-time identity |B_T|=N_T+L_T is algebraic from the residual definition; the mathematical construction content is its identification as the limit of independently defined curvature drifts and the proved positivity/monotonicity/continuity properties. The Gaussian sample space does not imply that every random variable in its L2 space is Gaussian. No Brownian-law assertion for N is being inferred from its covariance alone.

### What this establishes and what remains

This is a positive construction of a candidate local-time family in the actual L2 space. The monotonicity theorem is order on equivalence classes: for each fixed S<=T, the inequality holds almost surely. The continuity theorem is continuity into L2. Neither statement by itself supplies one jointly measurable version with continuous increasing sample paths for every time on a single probability-one event. In particular, L2 continuity plus monotonicity does not generally imply continuous sample paths.

A productive next construction is to realize the smooth drift approximants pathwise, identify their sections with these Bochner classes, and establish enough uniform-in-time control to construct a continuous limiting version. The support of its Stieltjes mass on Brownian zeros, occupation identities and the normalization required by a sticky clock still need proofs. ## Discoveries 463–464 — adapted envelopes and a finite-grid maximal estimate

Continued the actual Tanaka-path construction after461–462. The immediate obstacle was that fixed-time L2 convergence alone does not construct a uniform continuous path limit. Rechecked the current compensated-path representatives, raw-past conditional Ito theorem, and the pinned Mathlib conditional Jensen and discrete maximal-inequality interfaces.
