### 463 — construct an adapted nonnegative conditional envelope

`Foundation/ConditionalEnvelopeMaximal.lean` works on an arbitrary finite measure space with a discrete filtration. For a genuinely integrable terminal real function F, construct

E_i=max(E[|F||filtration_i],0).

The conditional-expectation process is an actual raw strongly adapted martingale. Its pointwise maximum with zero is an actual submartingale, nonnegative at every sample, satisfying the hypotheses of the pinned Mathlib `MeasureTheory.maximal_ineq` theorem. Conditional Jensen gives |E[F|filtration_i]|<=E_i almost surely. A separate theorem identifies E_i almost surely with the unmodified conditional expectation of |F|, so its integral is the actual terminal L1 norm.

Mathlib's discrete maximal inequality and positivity of the terminal envelope yield the verified bound

epsilon * measure{some i<=N has f_i>=epsilon} <= integral |F|

whenever each f_i is dominated almost surely by E_i. The countable conjunction of these domination events is justified explicitly before comparing the finite crossing events. The positive-part construction avoids pretending that an arbitrary almost-surely nonnegative representative is pointwise nonnegative. No adaptation of a chosen continuous modification is assumed merely from fixed-time almost-sure equality.

### 464 — specialize to the actual smooth compensated Brownian paths

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothGridMaximal.lean` constructs the discrete raw Brownian filtration at a monotone bounded sequence of times tau_i<=T. Its terminal function is the actual Gaussian-L2 class

F=M_n(T)-M_m(T),

where these M terms are the already constructed completed Ito integrals. The verified conditional Ito and horizon-cutoff formulas identify E[F|raw past at tau_i] with the difference of the actual continuous compensated paths at tau_i, almost surely. Thus their absolute differences are dominated by the constructed adapted envelope, with every required finite-measure, integrability and filtration hypothesis discharged.

A native Gaussian probability-space Cauchy–Schwarz argument proves integral|F|<=||F||_2. The actual integral isometry proves

||F||_2=||approximateField(n,T)-approximateField(m,T)||_2.

The resulting native finite-grid maximal probability estimate is

epsilon * P{there exists i<=N with |M_n(tau_i)-M_m(tau_i)|>=epsilon}
  <= ||approximateField(n,T)-approximateField(m,T)||_2.

The formal inequality uses nonnegative extended-real probability values and an ofReal conversion of the finite norm, so epsilon=0 is also covered without division by zero. It holds for every finite prefix of every monotone time sequence bounded by T. The right-hand side is independent of the grid size; the field sequence converges in the actual predictable L2 space by459. A weak L1 maximal bound is sufficient for a potential uniform-convergence-in-probability route; an L2 maximal inequality has not been asserted or needed for this result.

The theorem controls the actual already constructed continuous paths at a finite time grid. It does not yet prove a bound over every time in [0,T], nor construct a limiting continuous random path. One bounded monotone infinite time sequence is not itself a dense enumeration of the whole interval. Passing to all times requires a justified family of finite increasingly fine grids, continuity, measurable crossing events and probability limits. A fast subsequence and uniform-limit construction would then still be needed to obtain an actual continuous limiting version.

For the mass paths, the uniform scalar approximation bounds from458 must also be connected to differences of their compensated paths. ### 465 — arbitrary finite and countable time sets

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothFiniteSetMaximal.lean` removes the monotone-grid restriction from the finite event. A finite subset of [0,T] is sorted using its actual order embedding from Fin(cardinality), then extended constantly to a bounded monotone natural-time sequence. Every member of the finite set occurs in the controlled prefix, with no multiplicity or cardinality factor in the estimate. The empty set is handled separately.

For an arbitrary countable collection u_i<=T, the proof controls its finite prefixes and identifies their increasing union with the countable crossing event. Continuity of measure from below and multiplication through the extended-real supremum retain the same bound. This avoids the invalid shortcut of treating a single monotone bounded infinite sequence as a dense enumeration of an interval.

### 466 — the whole compact interval

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothCompactMaximal.lean` constructs a dense natural sequence in the nonempty separable subtype {t>=0:t<=T}. Every continuous compensated path difference that strictly exceeds epsilon at some time also strictly exceeds epsilon at a dense sample time. The converse is immediate from membership of the sample time in the interval. This proves an exact countable representation of the strict whole-interval crossing event and its measurability from the already proved coordinate measurability.

The countable maximal bound then gives the native compact-time estimate

epsilon * P{there exists t<=T with |M_n(t)-M_m(t)|>epsilon}
  <= ||approximateField(n,T)-approximateField(m,T)||_2.

The crossing event is strict: continuity and density do not automatically detect an isolated equality with a non-strict threshold. The implementation respects that distinction. The probability is evaluated on the actual continuous compensated paths, rather than on hypothetical path representatives of the abstract L2 limit.

### 467 — uniformly Cauchy in probability, including the mass paths

`Foundation/BrownianSmoothUniformCauchy.lean` proves the normalized uniform scalar estimate

|sqrt(x^2+e_n^2)-e_n-|x||<=e_n.

The actual path definitions then yield, for every sample and time,

|A_n(t)-A_m(t)|<=e_n+e_m+|M_n(t)-M_m(t)|.

This deterministic comparison also gives a compact-time maximal bound for mass-path crossings above epsilon+e_n+e_m. No uniform convergence of the curvature densities is assumed; they can concentrate as n grows.

Since the actual predictable coefficient sequence converges in L2, it is Cauchy. For positive epsilon and delta, its terminal norm difference is eventually less than epsilon*delta. Applying the compact estimate and cancelling the finite positive epsilon in extended-real arithmetic proves

### 468 — choose a fast increasing subsequence and prove one good event

`Foundation/BrownianMassFastSubsequence.lean` uses tolerance eta_j=2^(-j) and horizon j+1. The actual uniform-Cauchy theorem supplies a cutoff for every stage, with crossing probability below eta_j whenever both indices exceed that cutoff. A recursively defined subsequence takes the maximum of the next cutoff and the previous index plus1. Native theorems prove that it is strictly increasing and meets every corresponding cutoff.

The bad event at stage j is that the successive selected mass paths differ by more than eta_j somewhere before time j+1. Its probability is bounded by eta_j. The geometric series is summable, so native Borel–Cantelli proves a single probability-one event on which eventually, for every time t<=j+1, the successive selected paths differ by at most eta_j. The time quantifier is inside the good event; no invalid uncountable intersection of fixed-time almost-sure statements is used.

`Foundation/BrownianMassContinuousLimit.lean` first restricts selected paths to each compact interval [0,T]. The compact supremum distance between successive shifted paths is bounded by a geometric sequence. The verified geometric Cauchy theorem proves Cauchyness in the complete space of continuous functions on [0,T]; a shift does not affect Cauchyness.

The compact-open uniformity basis then proves that the selected entire paths are Cauchy in C(nonnegative reals,reals). Every compact time set is bounded by a finite T, so the preceding restrictions control every basic entourage. Completeness of the continuous-map space supplies an actual continuous limit path on each good sample. The preliminary choice is zero off the good event, and convergence of the measurable path sequence proves its almost-everywhere measurability. The standard measurable-version construction then yields an actual measurable map into the continuous-path space.

Native theorems prove that, almost surely, the selected mass paths converge to this map in compact-open topology, hence uniformly on every finite horizon simultaneously. On one probability-one event, the limit starts at zero, is monotone and is nonnegative for every time. These properties follow from the actual path convergence and the properties of the already constructed smooth paths, not from hypotheses supplied to a new stochastic object. The measurable-version replacement preserves the statements almost surely; it does not assert every bad sample has those order properties.

## Discoveries 471–474 — nontrivial atomless mass supported on Brownian zeros

Continued the productive pathwise Tanaka construction after the actual continuous limit468–470. The next independent mathematical question was whether this increasing residual really stays constant away from Brownian zeros, and whether the resulting zero-supported mass can be proved nontrivial. ### 471 — quantitative curvature concentration

`Foundation/BrownianCurvatureConcentration.lean` proves from the actual curvature formula that, for e>0 and delta>0,

delta<=|x| implies f''_e(x)<=e^2/delta^3.

The denominator estimate uses sqrt(x^2+e^2)>=|x|. Ordinary adjacent-interval integration identifies increments of the actual smooth mass paths with half the curvature integral on that interval. If a Brownian path stays at least delta away from zero on [s,t], then

0<=A_n(t)-A_n(s)<=(1/2)(t-s)e_n^2/delta^3.

Every term is from an independently constructed actual path integral. No support or occupation assertion is supplied to this estimate.

### 472 — no increase on zero-free compact intervals

`Foundation/BrownianMassZeroFreeIntervals.lean` passes that bound along the actual selected path subsequence. The width tends to zero and the selected path coordinates converge to the continuous limit, so the limiting increment is zero on every interval with a positive lower bound on |B|. On a compact zero-free interval, continuity of the actual Brownian path gives an attained strictly positive minimum of |B|. This supplies the lower bound rather than assuming one uniformly across samples.

The result holds on one probability-one event for every pair s<=t: if B_u!=0 for all u in [s,t], then L_s=L_t. A native contrapositive theorem proves that any strict increase of L across such an interval forces a Brownian zero somewhere in that interval. The all-interval quantifier follows pathwise from the existing good convergence event, not from an uncountable intersection of fixed-interval almost-sure events.

### 473 — construct the Stieltjes measure and prove support containment

`Foundation/BrownianMassStieltjesSupport.lean` constructs a genuine samplewise Stieltjes function from the continuous limiting path when it is monotone, and uses the constant-zero Stieltjes function otherwise. The good branch occurs almost surely by469. Both branches are continuous and monotone, so their native Stieltjes measures exist; continuity proves zero mass for every singleton, including time0.

The verified interval formula is, almost surely for all s,t,

mu_omega((s,t])=ofReal(L_t(omega)-L_s(omega)).

The corresponding closed-interval formula follows from the actual left-limit continuity. Hence zero-free compact intervals have zero Stieltjes mass. Around any nonzero Brownian value, continuity supplies a closed interval neighborhood contained in the zero-free open set. Its zero mass contradicts membership in the measure support. The native theorem consequently proves

support(mu_omega) subset {t>=0:B_t(omega)=0} almost surely.

Since the nonnegative time line is hereditarily Lindelof, the measure gives zero mass outside its support; the native concentration theorem therefore proves mu_omega{t:B_t!=0}=0. This is a full support/concentration statement for the constructed Stieltjes measure, stronger than just interval constancy. The module does not yet prove that omega->mu_omega is a measurable measure-valued kernel. The underlying continuous path map is already measurable; the samplewise measure construction and its support are what is formalized here.

`Foundation/BrownianMassNontriviality.lean` uses the actual nondegenerate Gaussian law at each T>0 to prove |B_T|>0 almost surely. The sign Ito integral is centered by456. The actual coordinate identification470 and genuine integrability then give

The native Stieltjes interval identity and L_0=0 identify the finite horizon mass with L_T almost surely. Thus E[mu_omega((0,T])]>0 for every positive T. This rules out an identically zero family. It does not claim that every sample has positive mass on every horizon, nor supply an explicit Gaussian expectation formula.

A formal mutual-singularity theorem relative to the chosen nonnegative-time Lebesgue measure would still need its measure-conversion details; no such extra Lean theorem is claimed here.

The full occupation/local-time identity, the relationship between the Tanaka convention and a specified sticky speed/reference parameter, measurability/adaptedness of the random inverse and strong Markov/sticky-generator identification remain unproved. ### 476 — the same-coordinate pushforward collapses to an atom

`Foundation/BrownianMassObservationCollapse.lean` constructs the actual finite-horizon measure obtained by pushing mu_omega restricted to [0,T] through the same continuous Brownian observation t->B_t(omega). ### 480. A reusable augmentation inside the given ambient sigma-algebra

## Discoveries 483–485 — exact clock-measure transport and nontrivial physical holding

### 483. Pushforward transport of the actual clock measure

`Foundation/BrownianClockMeasureTransport.lean` defines `ordinaryTime` on NNReal explicitly as the image of positive real Lebesgue measure under `Real.toNNReal`. This avoids silently postulating a new volume instance or replacing physical time with an arbitrary reference measure. `positive_preimage_Iic` and `ordinaryTime_Iic` identify every initial interval: its measure is exactly its endpoint.

`measure_ext_initial` is a reusable measure extensionality theorem on NNReal: finite values on initial intervals, and agreement there, imply equality of the full measures. Its proof uses the Borel-generating initial-interval pi-system and a natural-number exhaustion, so no unproved global-finiteness assumption is needed.

The actual mass Stieltjes measure satisfies `massMeasure_Iic ω t = mass ω t`, in ENNReal, at every sample, including the normalized fallback versions outside the almost-sure good set. `clockMeasure κ ω` is the genuine measure ordinaryTime + κ times massMeasure. `clockMeasure_Iic`, `forward_preimage_Iic` and `forward_map_clockMeasure` prove that its image under the actual forward clock is exactly ordinaryTime. This is a full equality of measures, not only a formal increment analogy or an assumed change-of-variables formula. Continuity, strict monotonicity and the already constructed inverse identities discharge its measurability and interval preimage obligations.

### 484. Exact occupation of zero after the random time change

`Foundation/BrownianStickyOccupation.lean` first proves `ordinaryTime_cut`, identifying restricted NNReal-time events with their real Lebesgue-time preimages. `brownian_zero_ordinary` transfers the verified original Brownian zero-occupation result to this measure; countable exhaustion yields a single good event for the entire half-line.

`zero_occupation` proves, on one probability-one event and simultaneously for every nonnegative κ and every nonnegative physical horizon T,

    ordinaryTime {t ≤ T : changedPath κ ω t = 0}
      = κ * mass ω (inverse κ ω T).

Its proof pulls the physical zero set back through the forward clock. The ordinary-time part vanishes by Brownian zero occupation; the singular mass part equals the whole mass of the inverse horizon because massMeasure is concentrated on Brownian zeros. `zero_occupation_gap` then uses the actual clock balance to identify this quantity with ENNReal.ofReal(T − inverse κ ω T). `zero_occupation_real` proves the same statement for real Lebesgue measure restricted to (0,T], applied to the genuine continuous changed path at `t.toNNReal`. The zero endpoint has no hidden contribution.

This closes the physical-time occupation obligation previously left open in482 for this constructed process and this exact clock coefficient. It does not identify the mass with an externally normalized local-time or Revuz convention, nor construct a transition law, strong Markov property or a stochastic flow.

The construction also resolves the apparent tension with454–455: original Brownian zero sets have zero ordinary time and cannot carry a nonzero ordinary-time density, yet their singular Stieltjes mass becomes positive physical occupation after the verified clock transport. The time measure changes; no absolute-continuity assumption or prohibited density shortcut has been used. The scalar spatial observation of this temporal mass still collapses to the Dirac measure at zero as shown in476; the new physical-time result does not turn it into a spatial Lebesgue diagonal measure for the manuscripts' multi-particle claims.

### 485. Holding is nontrivial at every positive deterministic horizon

`Foundation/BrownianStickyNontriviality.lean` defines `occupation` as the real value of the actual physical zero-set measure, not just as an independently specified clock gap. It is everywhere nonnegative; `occupation_gap` identifies it almost surely, simultaneously in κ and T, with T minus the actual inverse clock. `occupation_integrable` proves integrability for each parameter and horizon using that measurable bounded gap and its almost-everywhere identity.

`occupation_pos_iff` proves the useful order connection: for κ > 0, positive physical zero occupation by T is equivalent almost surely to positive constructed mass at the original Brownian time T. The strict inverse-clock threshold law, rather than independence of the clock and path, supplies this equivalence. `expected_occupation_pos` and `positive_occupation_probability` prove positive expected holding and positive probability of positive holding for every κ > 0 and every T > 0. They reuse the verified positive expectation of the constructed Brownian mass. They do not claim holding is almost surely positive at every such horizon. `occupation_parameter_zero` gives vanishing occupation for κ = 0, consistent with the recovered original Brownian path.

### Scope, remaining foundations and source provenance

The actual continuous Brownian time change now has the exact sticky-type physical occupation relation and nontrivial holding, in addition to the bounded inverse stopping-time and continuous-martingale foundations from480–482. This is a substantive realization result. A genuine sticky stochastic flow and instantiation of its transition semigroup/operator theory remain unproved: continuous-time sampling or stopped-process calculus, strong Markov/transition kernels, generator and boundary identification, matching to manuscript speed/diagonal conventions, compatible finite-particle laws and flow consistency still require independent proofs. Positive occupation alone does not supply these properties or establish equivalence with an external sticky model.

## Discoveries 488–490 — actual smooth strained Burgers vortex and the axial pressure boundary term

After the verified lattice checkpoint487, selectively screened existing source/report indices and returned to a distinct unresolved PDE question in `ResearchSources/Incoming/paper3_burgers_v1.tex`, SHA256 `A091CB020C8CB7838B27DD4157C98F14FCD0ACD5F61621AF39583C74B14195F1`. The justified question was whether the actual background strain changes the pressure contribution, a gap explicitly left open in229–231. No full manuscript ingestion or unverified helical sign assumption was used.

### 488. Reusable smooth parameter-integral profile calculus

`Foundation/GaussianSwirlProfileMoments.lean` constructs the actual scalar moment family

    moment(n,s) = (1/2) integral from0 to1 of (-t)^n exp(-t*s) dt.

`moment_hasDerivAt` proves its derivative is moment(n+1,s), for every natural n and every real s, by local dominated differentiation under the parameter integral. On the fixed interval, abs((-t)^(n+1)) ≤1 gives a common local exponential majorant. `moment_contDiff` and `moment_smooth` prove every finite derivative order and genuine C-infinity regularity. Degree0 is the previously constructed regular swirl profile h, and degree1 its actual derivative. The constructed radial pressure is also C-infinity. Differentiating the native curl identity gives

    4 h'(s) + 2 s h''(s) = -exp(-s).

The x/y chain rules needed for actual second spatial derivatives are proved. All statements include s=0; no quotient by radius or omitted vortex-axis case appears. This supplies a reusable analytic kernel family, rather than assuming the smoothness of a singular-looking quotient formula.

### 489. A genuine smooth stationary viscous profile, including the axis

`Foundation/StrainedBurgersVortex.lean` constructs, for real nu and gamma, s=x^2+y^2,

    u = (-2 nu x - gamma y h(s), -2 nu y + gamma x h(s), 4 nu z),
    p = gamma^2 P(s) - 2 nu^2 s - 8 nu^2 z^2,

where the already constructed radial pressure satisfies P'(s)=h(s)^2/2. For positive nu this is the matched stationary Burgers-vortex family with strain rate4nu and the specified Gaussian core width. Gamma is the amplitude parameter; no unproved circulation-normalization statement is attached to it.

`velocity_smooth` and `pressure_smooth` are joint C-infinity theorems on the actual three-dimensional real coordinate space. Native `HasDerivAt` theorems for all three velocity coordinates identify every displayed Jacobian entry with an actual partial derivative. The velocity is divergence-free. Its actual coordinate Laplacian is

    (2 gamma y exp(-s), -2 gamma x exp(-s), 0).

`stationary_navier_stokes` proves the stationary momentum equation (u dot grad)u + grad p = nu Delta u at every spatial point. `vorticity_eq` proves curl u = (0,0,gamma exp(-s)). These are actual smooth functions and derivative identities, not an affine surrogate, an assumed coefficient system or a generic conditional PDE theorem. The algebraic identities allow all real parameters; the positive-viscosity interpretation uses nu>0.

The independent standard-library finite-difference probe `.lake/stardust-489-probe.py` tested the momentum residual at the axis and two off-axis points, with nu=0.3 and gamma=1.2; residuals were below6e-9. The probe is explicitly numerical candidate evidence, not a formal theorem. The Lean derivative/PDE proofs provide verification independently of it.

### 490. Zero trace does not remove the strain-pressure boundary contribution

`Foundation/BurgersAxialPressureFlux.lean` defines the pressure Hessian from actual derivatives of the actual pressure gradient, and the vorticity Jacobian from actual vorticity derivatives. The diagonal pressure-Hessian entries are proved; `pressure_poisson` checks the full native compatibility trace(Hess p) = -trace((grad u)^2). Thus the pressure used for the test is both the verified momentum pressure and Poisson-compatible, not an arbitrarily chosen test pressure.

`trace_square_zero` verifies the genuine source symmetry identity trace((grad omega)^2)=0. At the same time, `hessian_zz`, `contraction_eq` and `contraction_neg` prove

    omega dot (Hess p) omega = -16 nu^2 gamma^2 exp(-s)^2 <0

when nu and gamma are nonzero. The straight vortex is not pointwise pressure-neutral in this strained family. There is no contradiction with the trace identity: the axial pressure is quadratic and contributes a nonzero boundary flux.

`axial_integral_boundary` proves the exact finite-interval relation

    integral from a to b of omega dot (Hess p) omega dz
      = [omega_z^2 partial_z p] at b minus its value at a.

`unit_slab_contraction` and `trace_does_not_cancel_slab` give an explicit nonzero unit-slab pressure integral while the corresponding integral of p times trace((grad omega)^2) vanishes. These are axial interval integrals at fixed x,y. They are not silently substituted for the source's whole-space or torus integrals. `axial_unbounded_above` proves that the actual velocity is unbounded along the axis when nu is nonzero, and `axial_unit_not_periodic` proves failure of axial unit periodicity.

## Discoveries 493–495 — actual phase-dependent pressure pairing, absolute integrability and both Fubini orders

Continued the productive proof from492 without further manuscript ingestion. Source relevance remains the pressure/trace and neutrality discussion85–151 of `ResearchSources/Incoming/paper3_burgers_v1.tex`, SHA256 `A091CB020C8CB7838B27DD4157C98F14FCD0ACD5F61621AF39583C74B14195F1`. That gap is now closed for the prescribed base-pressure/repaired-trace pairing, with its true product integrability proved.

### 493. Parity and genuine Gaussian-to-volume transport

`Foundation/GaussianPlaneParity.lean` proves that the physical quarter-variance product Gaussian is preserved by simultaneous transverse negation. It proves the corresponding odd-integral identity and the zero pairing of any even plane function with x*sin(theta)-y*cos(theta). Actual pressure applications separately establish integrability; the generic Bochner odd-integral identity is not used to replace a missing domain proof.

`weighted_integrable` and `weighted_integral` transport integrable functions under the actual density (2/pi)*exp(-2(x^2+y^2)) to the ordinary plane volume integral weighted by the squared Gaussian vortex profile. `phase_integrable` uses actual Gaussian L2 pressure membership and the verified coordinate-weight estimates. Consequently the linear-trace pressure pairing is genuinely integrable and zero for every even pressure cross-section. The reusable result does not require axial independence or periodic pressure.

### 494. The actual phase-dependent base pressure has a constant transverse pairing

`Foundation/BurgersRepairedTracePairing.lean` uses the actual function P(nu,gamma,theta)(x,y), with theta in its axial pressure term, and the native Jacobian of the already constructed solenoidal repaired vorticity field. The integrand is exactly pressure times trace((grad correctedOmega)^2), not a frozen plane surrogate.

The actual pressure is even under simultaneous x,y negation. The native trace splits into epsilon times the odd linear trace plus4*epsilon^2*profile^2*R, where R=2(x^2+y^2)-1. For every theta, the first pairing vanishes by transverse parity. The quadratic pairing is the verified radial observation; the axial quadratic pressure is a constant in each cross-section and contributes zero against the centered radial weight. Every transverse integral is proved integrable.

`crossSection_exact` proves that its value is independent of theta and equals

    (pi/2)*epsilon^2*[gamma^2*log(9/8)-4*nu^2].

The axial cross-section function is interval-integrable, and its exact integral on any real oriented interval a..b is (b-a) times that value. This is an exact polynomial-in-epsilon identity for the prescribed base pressure, not an assumed asymptotic O(epsilon^2) estimate.

### 495. Absolute integrability on the product space and genuine Fubini

`Foundation/BurgersPhaseProductIntegral.lean` constructs the actual restricted axial measure volume on(a,b] and proves it finite. The raw three-variable integrand is decomposed natively into six separated plane-times-axial terms. The plane coefficients are profile-squared times pressure-weighted coordinates, coordinates alone, the radial-pressure product and the radial weight alone. Their integrability comes from493 and the actual Gaussian pressure domain. The axial factors are continuous trigonometric/polynomial functions on finite intervals.

`joint_integrable` proves absolute Bochner integrability with respect to ordinary plane volume times the restricted axial Lebesgue measure whenever a≤b. This supplies the hypotheses of native Fubini, rather than inferring joint integrability from finite iterated values. `product_integral_exact`, `period_product_exact` and `phase_first_exact` identify the genuine product integral and both integration orders. On the finite phase interval0..2pi the result is

    pi^2*epsilon^2*[gamma^2*log(9/8)-4*nu^2].

Thus the value anticipated by the frozen-z functional492 is now independently justified for the actual phase-dependent base-pressure trace integrand. No pressure periodicity is assumed merely because the integration interval has length2pi. The domain is explicitly the plane times a finite axial interval.

### 496. The complete actual base-pressure Hessian

`Foundation/BurgersRepairedHessian.lean` proves both mixed transverse Hessian entries by differentiating the actual gradient of the actual Burgers pressure. They equal4*gamma^2*x*y*h(s)*h'(s), s=x^2+y^2. `hessian_eq` identifies the entire Hessian: the verified Dxx,Dyy on its transverse diagonal, these equal mixed entries, zero axial mixed entries and the axial entry-16*nu^2.

The mixed entry is measurable and has the actual bound abs(mixed) ≤ gamma^2*s/4. Its Gaussian integrability follows from this bound and the previously constructed radius-square pressure domain. No assumed Hessian model or singular division at the vortex axis is used.

    E[Dxx] = E[Dyy] =4*[gamma^2*log(9/8)/4-nu^2],   E[mixed]=0.

### 498. Absolute product integrability, exact Hessian pairing and literal boundary flux

`Foundation/BurgersHessianProductIntegral.lean` proves each transverse contraction integrable and evaluates it independently of the axial parameter. `axial_self_advection_zero` proves the unexpected cancellation

The flux jump is integrable on the entire plane. ## Discoveries 499–500 — exact conditional-update entropy and finite boundary obstructions

At the natural proof break following498, returned to the broader archive rather than extending the Burgers calculation indefinitely. Selected `ResearchSources/Incoming/entropy_ym (4).tex`, SHA256 `09827CC13CAFF0713CBE62B049BAE3B344DFB995E85A1D0DCAC38E4370E96D03`. Read only the theorem statements around131–215 and, for the precise question below, the complete short KL-chain-rule proof at403–417. A bounded keyword index located those passages. No other full manuscript proof was ingested and no instruction in the source was acted on. The concrete question was whether an exact conditional-entropy recursion itself supplies a positive dissipation fraction for the actual finite-word SU(2) conditional-resampling kernel constructed at444–445.

### 499. A native bridge from the actual update kernel to measure-theoretic relative entropy

New module: `Foundation/ConditionalResamplingEntropy.lean`,15 public declarations. This uses Mathlib's existing measure-theoretic `InformationTheory.klDiv` and composition-product chain rule; it does not reimplement relative entropy or replace it by a formal scalar variable. Let K be a Markov kernel from a measurable boundary space P to an interior space E, and U its verified boundary-preserving conditional-resampling update. For a finite joint law J and finite boundary reference tau:

    KL(U J || tau compProd K) = KL(J.fst || tau).

For another Markov conditional L and finite boundary law pi, the exact decomposition is:

    KL(pi compProd L || tau compProd K)
      = KL(U(pi compProd L) || tau compProd K)
        + KL(pi compProd L || pi compProd K).

`entropy_decomposition_of_conditional` also gives this statement for an actual joint J supplied with its conditional kernel L. These equalities are in ENNReal, so they remain meaningful for infinite divergence and require neither illegal infinity subtraction nor finiteness of the log-likelihood integral. The additive chain rule is the genuine identity; writing W_after = W_before - D or dividing by W requires the additional finiteness and nonzero assumptions appropriate to that operation.

Every pi compProd K is stationary under U. If pi differs from tau, its entropy against tau compProd K is strictly positive, whereas its conditional entropy against pi compProd K is exactly zero. `no_positive_dissipation_fraction` proves the failure of every strictly positive multiplicative conditional-dissipation lower bound on this whole class. This is stronger than merely observing nonuniqueness of stationary laws: it identifies the exact surviving entropy as boundary information.

The obstruction is also realized by actual probability measures with finite positive entropy. Define binaryReference(a,b) = (dirac(a)+dirac(b))/2. Native proofs establish probability normalization, dirac(a) absolutely continuous with respect to that reference, distinctness for measurable distinct atoms, finite KL of the corresponding composition-products and strictly positive real KL. `binary_no_strict_contraction` disproves every real factor q<1 for this explicit pair under U. `bool_counterexample` instantiates the distinct atoms as false and true, without an assumed existence of a nontrivial boundary. These are genuine measures and an actual kernel update, not an abstract entropy recurrence.

### 500. Instantiation for the constructed SU(2) interaction and Haar-based heat bath

New module: `Foundation/SU2HeatBathEntropy.lean`,6 public declarations. `actual_joint_entropy_after_update` identifies the relative entropy of any finite joint input after the actual finite-word SU(2) heat-bath update, **against the previously constructed globally normalized interaction law**, with the entropy of its original boundary marginal against the actual interaction boundary marginal. `actual_joint_entropy_decomposition` supplies the full additive identity for an actual input composition-product pi compProd L. These use the native joint factorization, boundary probability and measurable Markov kernel; the SU(2) objects are not replaced by a convenient scalar model.

`binary_boundary_obstruction` specializes the finite positive-entropy obstruction to the same SU(2) conditional kernel for a finite boundary index space. `opposite` is the actual determinant-one unitary matrix rotation(pi) = -I, and `one_ne_opposite` proves it differs from I by inspecting a matrix entry. `concrete_haar_obstruction` uses the actual quaternionically constructed Haar law for the resampled link, the explicit boundary configurations constantly I and constantly -I on Unit, any finite collection of words, any real interaction beta, and any q<1.

Scope distinction: the concrete obstruction's reference is **the two-atom boundary probability composed with the actual Haar-based conditional kernel**. It is not identified with the original Haar-boundary globally normalized Wilson-type joint law. The first two theorems address that original joint law directly, but no finite nonzero boundary-tilt witness relative to its continuous boundary marginal is newly constructed here. No universal strict contraction for a boundary-preserving update can be inferred merely from its conditional chain rule. This does not refute the manuscript's specific0.527 dissipation assertion for its selected RG measures, which may have additional structure; those quantitative and uniform hypotheses remain unverified.

Independent diagnostic: `.lake/stardust-500-probe.py` evaluates a two-sign SU(2) model with an atomic, rather than Haar, base law. For beta0,0.5,2,8, the stationary boundary-tilt entropy is approximately log(2), the conditional dissipation is0, and a separate input with incorrect conditionals obeys the additive decomposition to at most3.6e-15 floating error. This is numerical testing only; the native theorems establish the exact finite-positive obstruction without asserting a new native evaluation of its entropy as log(2). No Haar quadrature is claimed.

### Source assessment and next mathematical questions

The source's short chain-rule proof403–417 correctly identifies the coarse reference as the exact boundary marginal of the fine reference. Its formula is a genuine identity with these hypotheses, and its nonnegative conditional term supplies monotonicity. Neither a positive fixed loss fraction nor scale-uniform geometric decay follows from that identity alone. Applying it along a proposed RG construction requires verifying that each separately specified coarse reference is indeed that marginal, plus the quantitative conditional-entropy lower bound for the actual family. Gaussian/Schur analogies and an algebraic factorization do not by themselves discharge these obligations.

Useful next directions are a bounded-density boundary tilt relative to the actual continuous SU(2) interaction boundary law, or a genuinely boundary-changing overlap/sweep kernel whose information loss can be tested. A single fixed-boundary conditional heat bath should not be silently substituted for such a sweep or an RG map. The exact Schur and Hodge results, repaired Burgers boundary-flux identity, stochastic realizations and missing sticky multiparticle/Markov-generator foundations retain their earlier scopes. No Yang–Mills continuum gap, NS/YM equivalence or Millennium conclusion is established. Continue the indefinite discovery loop across the archive and verified library; do not turn these remaining entropy questions into mandatory completion requirements.

### 501. Actual conditioning and its exact finite KL divergence

New module: `Foundation/ConditioningRelativeEntropy.lean`,7 public declarations. Reuses Mathlib's actual conditional probability `ProbabilityTheory.cond mu s = (mu s)^(-1) smul mu.restrict s`. For a probability measure mu, measurable s and mu(s)>0, the native Radon–Nikodym and log-likelihood calculations prove:

    llr(mu restricted to s, mu) = 0 almost everywhere on the restriction;
    llr(cond(mu,s), mu) = log((mu(s)^(-1)).toReal) almost everywhere under cond(mu,s);
    KL(cond(mu,s) || mu) is finite;
    KL(cond(mu,s) || mu).toReal = log((mu(s)^(-1)).toReal).

When mu(s)<1, the conditional law differs from mu and its real KL divergence is strictly positive. These use the existing RN restriction/scaling, probability normalization and Gibbs identity, with all absolute-continuity and integrability hypotheses discharged. The infinite-value edge cases are excluded explicitly by positive event mass and the probability-measure assumption. The construction is a normalized restriction of the original law, not an atomic replacement or a free entropy variable. It also gives the elementary bounded-density construction suggested at500; no smoothness or strict positivity of the perturbing density is claimed.

### 513. The actual exponential convolution is not a martingale in its natural history

New module: `Foundation/GaussianVolterraMartingaleObstruction.lean`,12 public declarations. Reuses the actual process class `GaussianExponentialMarkovPrediction.value`, previously identified with the actual deterministic-profile Itô integral

### Source assessment and the missing obligation

The source's Volterra-Girsanov correction describes the effect of changing the driver measure. An ordinary martingale condition for a memory-driven quantity also requires control of the memory factor's intrinsic conditional behavior under the chosen measure. In the explicit exponential-kernel case, that behavior is already nonmartingale under the original law, without any new measure-change correction. ### 515. Actual time integration of the deterministic response profiles

New module: `Foundation/ExponentialResponseTimeIntegral.lean`,9 public declarations. Reuses the actual TimeHilbert=L2(Lebesgue) profile

    k_t(u)=1_(0,t](u)*exp(-lambda*(t-u)),

with lambda>0. The time parameter curve is already known to be norm-continuous. Construct a genuine jointly measurable triangular scalar kernel on(s,u), whose time slices are actual representatives of k_s. For s in(0,T], its absolute value is dominated by the fixed L2 majorant1_(0,T](u). This majorant has finite support in Lebesgue time; no constant majorant on the entire infinite Lebesgue line is assumed integrable.

The scalar column calculation is proved by ordinary FTC, with the triangular support and endpoint cases treated explicitly:

    integral_(0,T] k_s(u) ds
      = lambda^(-1)*(1_(0,T](u)-k_T(u)).

An independently supplied L2 class on the right has its actual representative proved by the Lp scalar/subtraction identities. The existing `BochnerL2Fubini.integral_eq_of_slices` theorem then identifies the actual Bochner integral, after verifying integrability, joint measurability, slice formulas and the L2 majorant:

    integral_0^T responseVector(lambda,s) ds
      = lambda^(-1)*(timeVector(T)-responseVector(lambda,T)).

The right side is not taken as the definition of the time integral. Its equality to that integral is the new proved fact. The lambda>0 hypothesis is substantive; this formula is not asserted by evaluating a totalized inverse at lambda=0.

### 516. Transport to the actual Gaussian stochastic-integral realization

New module: `Foundation/GaussianVolterraDriftBalance.lean`,14 public declarations. The actual isonormal embedding is the composition of the constructed Hilbert-coordinate embedding and the verified Gaussian first-chaos isometry. The actual exponential convolution Z_t is identified with the image of its actual response vector under this isometry. Its norm continuity, finite-interval Bochner integrability and the actual primitive

    P_T = integral_0^T Z_s ds

are established. The continuous linear isometry commutes with this actual Bochner integral, so515 yields the exact Gaussian-L2 identity

    P_T = lambda^(-1)*(B_T-Z_T),
    Z_T + lambda*P_T = B_T,

where B_T is the already constructed Brownian L2 class `GaussianTimeProcess.wienerL2 T`. This is not a new assigned driving noise. It is the actual image of the interval indicator in the existing Gaussian realization.

Define the actual drift primitive D_T=-lambda*P_T. Native FTC in Gaussian L2 proves

    D'_T = -lambda*Z_T,
    Z_T = B_T+D_T,
    Z_T-D_T = B_T.

The derivative is a Gaussian-L2 derivative, not a derivative of Brownian sample paths. Its exact squared norm is

    norm(D'_T)^2 = lambda*(1-exp(-2*lambda*T))/2.

It is strictly positive for every lambda>0,T>0. Thus the intrinsic ordinary-time term is concretely nonzero at the displayed Hilbert-space derivative level; it is not merely inferred from failure of a conditional expectation identity. The new `zero_rate_value` separately proves that the zero-rate convolution equals the actual Brownian L2 class, so the positive-rate memory term and the constant-kernel case are kept distinct.

### 524 — actual smooth periodic Navier–Stokes shear solutions

New module `Foundation/SpectralShearHeatFlow.lean`, namespace `OperatorDerivativeRewrite.Foundation.SpectralShearHeatFlow`, constructs an actual finite Fourier family with arbitrary natural high frequency n. For q=exp(-nu*t), r=exp(-nu*n²*t), its literal real velocity and pressure are

    u(t,x) = (2q sin(x₁) + q sin(x₂) + r sin(n x₁), 0, 0),   p=0.

`high_realization` and `velocity_formula` identify the synthesized Fourier field with this formula. The actual ordinary time derivative and the existing actual coordinate Laplacian are identified in `time_derivative`. `advection_zero`, `incompressible` and `momentum` prove the literal NS equation with pressure0. `periodic` proves period2π in every spatial coordinate; `velocity_smooth` proves joint C∞ regularity in real time and space. The profile's Hermitian symmetry is proved. General Fourier `lap_single`, the high-mode Laplacian and the profile Laplacian provide the spectral calculations. These are actual PDE solutions, not independently prescribed modal energy curves. The PDE identities hold for all real nu,t; the manuscript comparison uses positive viscosity and nonnegative time.

### 525 — a reusable normalized-shell invariant

New module `Foundation/NormalizedShellHeat.lean`, namespace `OperatorDerivativeRewrite.Foundation.NormalizedShellHeat`, works for every finite angular index set. No claim of nonlinear transfer, approximate equal shell frequencies or angular mixing is assumed. This distinguishes decay of absolute shell energies from change of their normalized proportions.

In525 the parameter named `frequency` denotes the squared-wavenumber shell centroid κ. In524 the `decay` parameter is the wavenumber itself and is squared inside its exponential. These conventions give the same physical energy factor exp(-2*nu*κ*t).

under the explicit positive/nondegenerate hypotheses used by the actual field. `centroid_gt_one` and `actual_sourceRatio_gt_one` prove that this ratio is strictly above1 for every n≥2, every real viscosity and every finite real time. ## Stardust checkpoint 1149 — uniform signed CENTRAL Gaussian approximation in the transition region (October 20, 2026)

A(4) remains active. Building on the constructed ACTUAL arithmetic saddles, this checkpoint proves a signed central-integral approximation with a rigorously nonzero full complex Gaussian normalization, and proves its relative error tends to zero uniformly at each fixed bounded frequency-to-scale ratio. The word CENTRAL is essential: the actual integral is over a shrinking horizontal neighborhood of the actual saddle. The Gaussian comparison is over the whole real line. This is not yet a bound for the complete actual horizontal integral, the paired transform, its zeros, or global re-entry.

New root-imported module: Foundation/RiemannQuarticTransitionGaussian.lean. It reuses TransitionCorrection, the generic real ODE identity normalized_real_ode, the existing leadingPhase and its exact primitive identity, the existing exponential cubic remainder, the complex Gaussian integral and oscillatory tail estimate, and the already verified centralRadius(Q)=Q^(-7/16) and its power limits. No new integration, Gaussian, or analytic-inverse foundation is introduced. Some common section hypotheses are deliberately retained even on a few auxiliary estimates that need fewer of them; actual public types were reviewed with those hypotheses present.

The common data are t>=1, K>=8, a=Re(w)>=1000, abs(Im(w))<=1/2, norm(w)<=2*a, Im(c)<=1, the MODEL equation D_t(w)=-i*c, norm(exp(4*w))<=K, and an ACTUAL integration center v with norm(v-w)<=1/K. Set Q=t*a^3 and E=30005*exp(-4*a+4). The actual frequency z need not equal c in the intermediate estimates; the actual stationarity equation G_t(v)=-i*z is explicitly required for the Gaussian approximation.

horizontal_neighbor_domain proves the arithmetic kernel domain on the FIXED real interval abs(s)<=1/16 about v, with Re(exp(4*(v+s)))>=Q/64 and Re(v+s)>=0. It reuses the corrected double-ball domain and the generic positive real exponential translation bound. horizontal_neighbor_error strengthens the arithmetic/model slope error there to E. The proof directly bounds the theta remainder on the interval. It does not take high-order Cauchy derivatives on the tiny radius-1/K correction ball, which could introduce unnecessary powers of K.

horizontal_slope_continuousOn and horizontal_weight_hasDerivAt prove the actual slope continuity and actual arithmetic weight ODE, including the nonzero denominator. actual_horizontal_phase then applies the existing generic normalized real ODE to obtain EXACTLY W(v+s)=W(v)*exp(integral_0^s(G_t(v+r)+i*z)dr). actual_phase_model_error proves the complex phase integral differs from leadingPhase by at most E*abs(s). All phase and weight identities are actual signed complex identities, not expectation-level heat formulas or absolute-value replacements of the integral.

corrected_exp_norm gives norm(exp(4*v))<=2*K. corrected_polynomial_scale gives t*(4*norm(v)+1)<=K. model_real_curvature separately proves Re(D_t'(v))<=-3*Q. Thus the model Gaussian has positive real decay coefficient b=-D_t'(v)/2, and its exponential has norm at most one on the entire real displacement line. No claim of decay is inferred merely from nonzero complex curvature.

The existing explicit exponential cubic remainder gives leadingPhase_cubic_bound with error 2048*K*norm(s)^3 after subtracting both its LINEAR and quadratic terms. At an actual saddle the model linear term is NOT zero: D_t(v)+i*z=-(G_t(v)-D_t(v)), and its norm is bounded by E. leadingPhase_quadratic_bound retains this term. Combining it with the actual/model phase error yields actual_phase_quadratic_bound: the ACTUAL integrated phase differs from D_t'(v)*s^2/2 by at most 2*E*abs(s)+2048*K*abs(s)^3.

If 0<=r<1/16 and 2*E*r+2048*K*r^3<=1, actual_quadratic_weight_error and actual_local_quadratic_error rigorously compare the SIGNED actual integral over [-r,r] with the signed truncated complex Gaussian times W(v). The bound is (8*E*r^2+8192*K*r^4)*norm(W(v)). The proof first obtains a pointwise complex exponential difference bound, then integrates the signed difference; it never infers cancellation bounds from an expectation or replaces the signed target by an integral of absolute values.

## Checkpoint1267: global finite-shift strip contraction, with multiplicities

Foundation/SymmetricPolynomialStrip.lean independently verifies the finite-
polynomial symmetric imaginary shift argument. The operator is ACTUALLY
  S_h(P)(z)=(P(z+i*h)+P(z-i*h))/2.
For ANY nonzero conjugation-fixed complex polynomial (hence any nonzero real
polynomial mapped to C), h>0, and ANY real b such that ALL initial zeros satisfy
(Im a)^2<=b^2, EVERY zero of S_h(P) satisfies
  (Im z)^2<=max(b^2-h^2,0).
Constants are handled separately; no positive-degree premise is hidden in the
final strip theorem. The output remains nonzero and conjugation-fixed. Generic
b need not be nonnegative, since its square is the stated budget. The zero
polynomial is explicitly excluded, as the verified negative control requires.

The key exact identity for each conjugate root pair is the difference of the
products of squared norms at z+i*h and z-i*h:
  8*h*Im(z)*((Re(z)-Re(a))^2+Im(z)^2+h^2-Im(a)^2).
Above the target strip it is strictly positive. The proof multiplies comparisons
over the COMPLETE ROOT MULTISET, including repeated roots. Conjugation permutes
that multiset with ALL multiplicities, by the existing splitting/root-map
machinery. Pair products over the full multiset become squares of the original
norm products; nonnegativity justifies recovering the strict comparison. The
fundamental theorem of algebra supplies the exact polynomial/root product and
nonzero leading coefficient. The upper half-plane comparison forbids cancellation;
conjugation gives the lower half-plane. No root enumeration by time, simple-root
premise, discriminant premise, velocity or unproved collision continuation occurs.

The finite iteration theorem is GLOBAL: for EVERY natural n, S_h iterated n
times remains nonzero and conjugation-fixed, and every zero satisfies
  (Im z)^2<=max(b^2-n*h^2,0).
The proof carefully clips the budget at zero at each step; max(max(B,0)-q,0)=
max(B-q,0) for q>=0. This verifies all-real preservation after the budget is
spent. Repeated roots, switches of uppermost roots and arbitrary degrees are
included directly in this static finite-shift result.

For fixed REAL s>0, define scaledShift(s,n,P) using n+1 repetitions of
h=sqrt(2*s/(n+1)). The clock (n+1)*h^2=2*s is proved, with no zero denominator.
EVERY n therefore has the SAME bound max(b^2-2*s,0), remains nonzero and has
real coefficients in the exact conjugation-fixed sense. An explicit wrapper
instantiates actual real polynomials via coefficientwise complexification.
All roots are real when b^2<=2*s. These statements are about FINITE SHIFTS.
The s=0 identity is checked separately; positive-s scaling theorems do not
silently include that boundary through a false strict-positive shift premise.

The missing next theorem is STILL the scaling limit
  scaledShift(s,n,P) -> (transport2(-s)P)_C
locally uniformly on C for each fixed finite real polynomial P.1266 identifies
the RIGHT-HAND SIDE with actual Gaussian heat, but does not identify it with
each FINITE symmetric shift. An explicit checked quartic distinguishes them:
for P(z)=(z^2+1)^2, S_1(P)=z^2(z^2-4), hence S_1(P)(0)=0, whereas the genuine
imaginary Gaussian heat at s=1/2 has value2 at0. Thus finite-shift control cannot

## Checkpoint1268: polynomial-specific Euler limit in the existing jet norm

Foundation/NilpotentVectorEuler.lean proves a finite-vector Euler theorem using
existing Mathlib binomial asymptotics and Banach exponential. Let E be a complete

commutation of A_n for different n, positivity, a new probability law, nor a
new function-space completion is required. D=0 is admitted and forces v=0.

therefore permits a FINITE sum limit. The limit B also kills v at power D,
proved by continuity and uniqueness of limits, not added as an assumption.
The genuine existing exponential series, mapped by continuous evaluation at v,
then reduces to that same finite sum. The preliminary finite-sum theorem needs
